new_roles.title: Manufacturing Quality Director
new_roles.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.  

 The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities:  we come together ,  we always look for a better way , and  we create possibilities . 

 Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

 Interested in joining us on our journey? 

The Manufacturing Quality Director provides strategic leadership and oversight of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational excellence, product reliability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement. This position is responsible for developing and executing quality strategies, driving improvements in internal and external quality metrics, and reducing the overall cost of quality.
As a key member of the plant leadership team, the Manufacturing Quality Director partners with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Product Management, Supplier Quality, Technology, Distribution, and Service to establish quality objectives, resolve complex quality issues, and ensure alignment with business priorities.
The Director is accountable for manufacturing quality performance, execution of the quality operating plan, continuous improvement initiatives, and leadership and development of the Quality organization.
This role supports plant operations in LaFayette, GA. 
 Position 
Manufacturing Quality Director 
 Location 
USA, LaFayette, GA 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Quality Strategy and Operational Leadership 
 Develop and execute manufacturing quality strategies aligned with plant and business objectives.
 Provide leadership and direction for quality performance across manufacturing operations.
  
 Establish measurable quality objectives, performance targets, and improvement plans to support operational excellence.
 Partner with plant leadership and cross-functional teams to integrate quality requirements into manufacturing processes and business decisions.
 Drive accountability for quality performance through effective communication, performance reviews, and corrective action plans.
 Promote a culture of quality ownership, continuous improvement, and proactive problem-solving throughout the organization.
  
 Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement 
  
 Own and drive improvement of key internal and external quality metrics, including First Pass Yield (FPY), Cost of Quality (COQ), Service Call Rate (SCR), scrap, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), and product damage.
 Analyze quality performance data to identify trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.
 Lead the development and execution of corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans to address quality concerns and prevent recurrence.
 Ensure timely containment, root cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions for End-of-Line Audit (EOLA) findings and other manufacturing quality issues.
 Drive year-over-year improvements in quality performance, process capability, and manufacturing efficiency.
 Champion Lean principles, structured problem-solving, error-proofing (poka-yoke), and proactive quality tools to reduce defects and improve process reliability.
  
 Cost of Quality and Financial Accountability 
 Own the development and execution of the manufacturing Cost of Quality operating plan.
 Identify and prioritize opportunities to reduce scrap, rework, warranty exposure, product damage, and other quality-related costs.
 Establish improvement initiatives targeting the highest contributors to quality losses.
 Partner with Operations, Finance, Engineering, and other stakeholders to evaluate financial impacts and deliver sustainable cost reductions.
 Monitor performance against quality cost targets and implement corrective actions to address unfavorable trends.
 Drive resolution of quality-related concessions attributable to manufacturing operations and implement strategies to prevent recurrence.
  
 Quality Management Systems and Process Control 
 Ensure manufacturing operations comply with established Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, applicable ISO standards, and internal quality procedures.
 Provide oversight of the Manufacturing Change Process (MCP), ensuring changes are appropriately evaluated, documented, approved, communicated, and implemented.
 Partner with the Change Implementation Board (CIB) and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain effective change control and documentation compliance.
 Identify critical manufacturing processes requiring control plans and ensure appropriate controls are established, documented, and maintained.
 Ensure manufacturing quality standards, procedures, and control plans remain current and are consistently followed.
 Support continuous improvement of quality systems, process controls, and manufacturing standards to minimize operational risk.
  
 Cross-Functional Quality and Customer Support 
  
 Collaborate with Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Product Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Field Quality, Distribution, and Service to resolve quality issues impacting manufacturing operations and customers.
 Partner with Supplier Quality to address supplier-related defects, assess proposed supplier changes, and ensure appropriate change control and production readiness.
 Work with Field Quality and Service organizations to identify emerging product concerns, evaluate field performance, and implement effective manufacturing countermeasures.
 Ensure appropriate quality controls are established for product rework, reprogramming, and corrective actions performed at supplier facilities, distribution centers, or other locations.
 Support resolution of Technical Assistance Group (TAG) concerns and other field service issues attributable to manufacturing processes.
 Collaborate with Engineering to recommend improvements to product testing requirements and manufacturing controls based on field performance and customer usage.
 Leverage technical expertise across the organization to accelerate problem resolution and achieve quality objectives.
  
 People Leadership and Organizational Development 
 Lead, develop, and manage the Manufacturing Quality organization, including Quality Leaders, Quality Engineers, technical specialists, and other supporting personnel.
 Establish clear performance expectations, responsibilities, and development objectives aligned with departmental and business priorities.
 Provide coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to strengthen technical capabilities, leadership effectiveness, and accountability.
 Ensure appropriate staffing, resource allocation, and prioritization of quality initiatives to meet operational requirements.
 Build a high-performing quality organization focused on collaboration, continuous improvement, and measurable results.
 Promote employee engagement, knowledge sharing, and the development of future quality leaders.
  
 Performance Monitoring and Business Reporting 
 Establish and maintain effective daily, weekly, and monthly quality performance reviews.
 Monitor key performance indicators, identify unfavorable trends, and ensure timely escalation and resolution of significant quality concerns.
 Communicate quality performance, improvement initiatives, risks, and corrective action progress to plant and business leadership.
 Translate complex quality data into actionable business insights and improvement priorities.
 Ensure quality initiatives are executed within established timelines, budgets, and performance expectations.
  
 Leadership Expectations 
  
 Demonstrate ownership and accountability for manufacturing quality performance.
 Influence decisions and drive results across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Balance immediate operational quality requirements with long-term strategic improvement objectives.
 Exercise sound judgment in evaluating quality risks, business impacts, and resource priorities.
 Foster collaboration, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.
 Develop organizational capability through effective leadership, talent development, and succession planning.
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline; equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience may be considered.
 Experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Reliability, Product Service, or a related technical function.
 Demonstrated experience with root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies.
 Ability to analyze technical and quality data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Demonstrated ability to work effectively across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical investigations simultaneously.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and PowerPoint.
 Knowledge of PFMEA, Control Plans, CAPA, SPC, and other quality systems and tools.
 Experience supporting New Product Introduction and product reliability initiatives.
   
 
 
 Our Culture 
 Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 

 This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 

 By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy. 
 
 
 
 GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization. 
 
 
 GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. 
 
 GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S 
 
 
 If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail to ask.recruiting@geappliances.com

existing_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Job Description:
The Compensation Director, Aircraft Engineering and Manufacturing, serves as the strategic compensation leader for the Aircraft division, providing enterprise-level oversight for compensation programs supporting manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades. This role defines compensation strategy for large, complex employee populations while ensuring programs are competitive, scalable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. 
As the organization's subject matter expert for manufacturing and operations compensation, the Director partners closely with business leaders, Px Business Partners, Finance, and Legal to design compensation programs that enable business growth, talent attraction, workforce scalability, and operational excellence. 
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in manufacturing compensation strategy, non-exempt workforce design, market intelligence, and executive consulting, with a demonstrated ability to influence enterprise decisions and build compensation frameworks that support rapidly growing operations. 

What you'll do:: 
 Compensation Strategy & Enterprise Leadership 


 Develop and lead the compensation strategy supporting Aircraft manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades populations. 

 Serve as the SME on manufacturing and operations compensation, shaping long-term compensation philosophy and governance. 

 Partner with business leadership to align compensation strategy with business growth, workforce planning, organizational design, and operational priorities. 

 Drive compensation initiatives supporting facility expansions, new business models, geographic growth, and workforce transformation. 


 Manufacturing & Operations Compensation 


 Lead the design and evolution of compensation structures supporting large non-exempt employee populations. 

 Establish wage structures, geographic differentials, shift premium strategies, progression frameworks, and other compensation programs that balance external competitiveness with internal equity. 

 Oversee market pricing methodologies utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys alongside complementary market intelligence. 

 Develop innovative compensation approaches to attract and retain highly competitive manufacturing, technical, and operational talent. 


 Executive Partnership & Business Consulting 


 Serve as the trusted compensation advisor to Aircraft executives and business leaders. 

 Consult on organization design, workforce investments, location strategy, and talent acquisition decisions with significant financial and organizational impact in partnership with the Px Business Partner. 

 Provide strategic guidance on compensation implications of organizational changes, acquisitions, new facilities, and business expansion. 

 Present compensation recommendations and analyses to executive leadership with clear business rationale and risk assessments. 


 Compensation Analytics & Insights 


 Lead enterprise compensation analyses including market competitiveness, pay equity, workforce cost modeling, and incentive effectiveness. 

 Translate complex compensation data into actionable insights for executive stakeholders. 

 Anticipate market trends and proactively recommend compensation strategies that strengthen organizational competitiveness. 


 Governance, Compliance & Program Excellence 


 Establish governance frameworks, policies, and administration standards for manufacturing compensation programs. 

 Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local wage and hour regulations while mitigating organizational risk. 

 Partner with Legal, Finance, and People Operations on complex compensation matters and regulatory changes. 

 Lead continuous improvement initiatives to simplify compensation processes, improve scalability, and enhance operational efficiency. 


 Leadership 


 Champion best practices in compensation design, analytics, governance, and operational excellence. 

 Build organizational capability through knowledge sharing, coaching, and development of compensation expertise across the People function. 




Required qualifications:: 

 Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Finance, Business, Economics, or a related field. 

 15+ years of progressive compensation experience, including significant leadership supporting manufacturing, production, operations, or supply chain organizations. 

 Deep expertise designing enterprise compensation strategies for large non-exempt employee populations. 

 Extensive knowledge of wage and hour regulations, compensation governance, and manufacturing compensation practices.

 Demonstrated experience designing wage structures, progression frameworks, geographic differentials, and premium pay programs. 

 Advanced analytical, financial modeling, and executive presentation skills. 

 Proven ability to influence senior executives and drive enterprise-wide compensation decisions. 

 Experience leading large, cross-functional compensation initiatives with significant organizational impact. 




Preferred qualifications:: 

 Certified Compensation Professional (CCP). 

 Experience supporting both union and non-union manufacturing environments. 

 Experience within global manufacturing or advanced technology organizations. 

 Expertise utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys. 

 Experience with Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, or enterprise compensation planning systems. 

 Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement experience. 

 Experience leading or mentoring compensation professionals.

 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing or a related technical field.

 Strong understanding of manufacturing readiness, tooling validation, material coordination and production launch. 

 Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery and cost through Lean manufacturing and structured problem-solving.

 Direct experience taking a new aircraft program from prototype through initial and rate production.

 Experience in aircraft final assembly, systems integration and production test.

We’re looking for a hands-on quality leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production. 
You will build the aircraft quality organization and establish the quality capability for our new Seattle-area production facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll own product and process quality across prototype, pre-series and production builds, ensuring that lessons from development become effective controls as the program scales. 
This role owns the Quality Management System, quality engineering, inspection, nonconformance management and audit readiness for the X-BAT manufacturing operation. You’ll partner with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Production and Supply Chain to prevent defects, resolve recurring problems and deliver aircraft that meet technical, customer and applicable regulatory requirements. 
We need a technically credible leader who can build practical, scalable systems, make sound decisions under schedule pressure and challenge senior stakeholders constructively while keeping execution moving. 

What you'll do:: 
 Build quality into prototype and launch 


 Lead quality planning and execution for X-BAT prototype and development builds, establishing appropriate inspection, test evidence and build records as designs evolve. 

 Partner with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering to identify product and process risks, define critical controls and build quality requirements into tooling, work instructions and test plans. 

 Establish configuration and traceability controls with Engineering and Production, ensuring each aircraft’s build status, deviations and nonconformances are understood and documented. 

 Capture lessons from build, integration and test issues, and drive their incorporation into design changes, manufacturing processes and future builds. 

 Define quality readiness criteria for pre-series builds and production launch, validating inspection methods, process controls, workforce competence and closure of significant risks. 


 Establish the Seattle quality operation 


 Recruit, develop and lead the quality team, building the technical capability and frontline support needed as aircraft production grows. 

 Establish and maintain a lean, effective QMS for X-Forge 3, aligned with Shield AI’s wider quality framework, AS9100, ISO 9001 and applicable customer requirements. 

 Lead certification readiness and internal, customer and external audits, driving timely closure and sustained effectiveness of corrective actions. 

 Set up receiving, in-process and final inspection capability, including measurement equipment, calibration, training and quality records, in partnership with relevant functions. 


 Deliver quality at rate 


 Own production quality performance, using first-pass yield, defects, rework and escapes to focus action where it improves aircraft quality and production flow. 

 Lead containment, root cause analysis and corrective action for manufacturing quality issues, with clear functional ownership and verification that fixes prevent recurrence. 

 Own the nonconformance and MRB process, ensuring disposition decisions follow approved technical authority and that affected hardware remains controlled. 

 Partner with Supply Chain and supplier quality teams to resolve incoming quality issues and improve supplier performance before defects disrupt aircraft builds. 

 Work with Engineering and Production to define acceptance evidence and ensure aircraft meet approved requirements before release. 

 Use digital quality tools and manufacturing data to strengthen traceability, expose trends and reduce manual administration as production scales. 

 Give leadership a clear view of quality performance, product risks and readiness; escalate or stop affected work when requirements or product integrity cannot be assured. 




Required qualifications:: 

 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality or a related technical field. 

 10+ years of leadership experience in quality, product assurance or reliability within aerospace, defense technology or high-reliability manufacturing. 

 Demonstrated success leading quality through prototype or new product introduction and into sustained production. 

 Proven ability to build and scale quality teams and systems while supporting fast-paced development and manufacturing operations. 

 Deep expertise in containment, root cause analysis, MRB, corrective and preventive action, and continuous improvement. 

 Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and ISO 9001, with practical implementation and audit leadership experience. 

 Experience with complex assembly, inspection, configuration control, traceability and product acceptance. 

 Ability to influence and challenge senior leaders constructively across Engineering, Production and Supply Chain. 

 A hands-on leadership style and sound technical judgment, balancing timely execution with clear quality standards and accountability. 




Preferred qualifications:: 

 Direct experience taking a new aircraft program from prototype through production launch and rate ramp. 

 Experience establishing quality capability at a new manufacturing facility or transferring production between sites. 

 Experience in aircraft final assembly, systems integration, production test and reliability improvement. 

 Experience deploying digital quality systems, statistical process controls and data-driven defect prevention. 

 Advanced degree in engineering, quality or a related technical discipline.

Job Description:
The Senior Manager of Quality is responsible for establishing and leading all quality activities for a complex aerospace development program from prototype through production readiness. This role serves as the primary quality leader embedded within the program team and partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Flight Test, and Program Management to ensure products are designed, developed, tested, and transitioned to production with quality, reliability, and mission success as foundational objectives.
The Senior Manager of Quality will build and lead a multidisciplinary quality team while implementing scalable quality systems, risk management processes, problem-solving disciplines, and development quality practices appropriate for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense technology organization.
This position requires balancing speed of development with disciplined engineering rigor to support aggressive program schedules while ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.

What you'll do:: 
 Development Quality Leadership 


 Serve as the quality leader for XBAT development.

 Establish quality strategy, objectives, and metrics aligned with program milestones.

 Integrate quality requirements into the product development lifecycle.

 Ensure quality considerations are incorporated during system architecture, design reviews, verification, validation, and qualification activities.

 Partner with Engineering leadership to identify and mitigate technical and programmatic risks.

 Drive a culture of proactive quality and continuous improvement throughout the program.


 Design & Configuration Quality 


 Ensure quality requirements are appropriately captured in product definitions, specifications, and design documentation.

 Participate in design reviews, change control boards, and configuration management activities.

 Ensure full configuration and traceability for all material installed into prototype aircraft.

 Evaluate engineering changes for quality and production readiness impacts.

 Support requirements verification and validation planning.

 Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-quality, and design-for-reliability initiatives.


 Risk Management & Reliability 


 Lead quality participation in program risk management activities.

 Establish and maintain FRACAS processes for development and flight test phases of the program.

 Facilitate root cause and corrective action investigations for design, manufacturing, supplier, and field failures.

 Support reliability growth planning and execution.

 Monitor defect trends, failure modes, and reliability metrics to identify systemic risks.


 Verification, Validation & Test Quality 


 Develop quality oversight strategies for laboratory, ground, and flight test activities.

 Ensure test results, anomalies, and nonconformances are appropriately documented and dispositioned.

 Support qualification and certification efforts.

 Establish processes for managing test escapes, failures, and corrective actions.


 Nonconformance & Corrective Action Management 


 Lead Material Review Board activities for development hardware.

 Establish scalable processes for nonconformance management.

 Drive root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methodologies.

 Ensure timely and effective corrective and preventive actions.

 Track effectiveness of corrective actions through closure.


 Production Readiness & Industrialization 


 Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to transition products from prototype to production.

 Define quality requirements for production readiness reviews.

 Support development of inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and control strategies.

 Ensure lessons learned from development are incorporated into production processes.

 Lead quality planning activities supporting low-rate initial production and rate increases.


 Quality Management System 


 Develop and implement quality processes supporting aerospace development programs.

 Ensure compliance with AS9100, customer requirements, and internal procedures.

 Drive continuous improvement of development quality processes.

 Support internal and external audits as required.

 Establish scalable systems that support future production growth.


 Leadership & Team Development 


 Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing quality organization.

 Recruit and develop quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians.

 Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.

 Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and collaboration.

 Develop organizational capabilities to support future company growth.




Required qualifications:: 

 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical discipline.

 10+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, space, or other highly regulated industries.

 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical quality organizations.

 Experience supporting complex product development programs from concept through production transition.

 Strong knowledge of quality systems, engineering development processes, and aerospace manufacturing.

 Experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action programs.

 Experience with risk management, reliability engineering, and failure analysis.

 Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems.

 Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.




Preferred qualifications:: 

 Experience supporting UAV, aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, or advanced technology programs.

 Experience leading quality organizations during rapid company growth.

 Background in systems engineering, reliability engineering, or development engineering.

 Experience with flight test programs and qualification testing.

 ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or equivalent certification.

 Familiarity with government defense programs and customer quality requirements.

Job Description:
 
Shield AI builds autonomy systems for defense applications, including air, maritime, and space platforms operating in complex and contested environments. 
We are building the AI Factory Reference Architecture, a Kubernetes-native platform for developing, training, evaluating, and deploying next-generation AI systems.
The AI Factory serves two purposes. Internally, it powers autonomy development across Hivemind and other AI programs. Externally, it becomes the reference architecture deployed into customer environments, spanning commercial cloud, on-premise infrastructure, sovereign deployments, and fully air-gapped systems.
We are looking for a Senior Staff Engineer to help define and build this platform. You will partner closely with ML researchers, platform engineers, and autonomy teams to deliver an exceptional developer experience for training and deploying modern AI models.
Success in this role requires balancing researcher productivity, platform simplicity, operational excellence, and long-term maintainability. You will work hands-on across the stack, helping shape both the platform architecture and its implementation while staying closely aligned with the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem. 

What you'll do:: 
 AI Platform Development: Lead the design and implementation of the AI Factory Reference Architecture, delivering a Kubernetes-native platform for AI development, distributed training, simulation, evaluation, and deployment.

 AI Research Enablement: Partner directly with ML researchers to understand evolving training workflows and ensure the platform supports state-of-the-art AI frameworks, foundation model development, reinforcement learning, distributed training, and emerging research workflows.

 Developer Experience: Design self-service AI development workflows that enable engineers to move seamlessly from local experimentation to large-scale distributed execution using familiar open source tools and frameworks.

 Distributed AI Infrastructure: Build the infrastructure required to support distributed training, simulation, inference, and reinforcement learning workloads. Evaluate and integrate orchestration, scheduling, and resource management technologies to maximize scalability and developer productivity.

 Compute Platform: Design and optimize shared GPU infrastructure across cloud and on-premises environments. Improve resource utilization, scheduling efficiency, storage, networking, observability, and overall platform reliability.

 Data & Model Lifecycle: Build platform capabilities that enable dataset management, experiment tracking, artifact management, model versioning, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous model improvement.

 Platform Distribution: Develop repeatable deployment and lifecycle management solutions using Infrastructure as Code and modern platform engineering practices. Support commercial cloud, customer-managed infrastructure, sovereign environments, and fully air-gapped deployments.

 Technology Leadership: Evaluate emerging AI infrastructure technologies and establish architectural patterns that balance scalability, performance, maintainability, and developer experience.

 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with AI researchers, autonomy teams, infrastructure engineers, and product teams to ensure the platform evolves alongside customer needs and advances in AI.


Key Outcomes:: 
 Engineers move from idea to distributed training in hours instead of days.

 High GPU utilization through efficient scheduling with KAI on Kubernetes.

 Researchers use modern AI tooling without unnecessary platform friction.

 AI Workspaces become the standard development environment across autonomy programs.

 Training, simulation, evaluation, and deployment operate as a unified platform.

 The AI Factory Reference Architecture can be deployed consistently across cloud, on-premise, and air-gapped environments.

 Platform capabilities are reusable across multiple autonomy programs and customer deployments.


Required qualifications:: 
 Experience building Kubernetes-native AI or MLOps platforms supporting distributed machine learning workloads.

 Deep understanding of modern AI training frameworks, including PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers and distributed training techniques.

 Experience operating GPU-accelerated infrastructure and distributed training systems.

 Strong understanding of Kubernetes, Linux, networking, security, storage, and distributed systems.

 Experience with GPU scheduling concepts and large-scale AI workloads.

 Experience packaging and deploying cloud-native infrastructure using Terraform and Helm.

 Strong software engineering skills in Python and Golang and modern cloud-native technologies.

 Experience collaborating closely with ML researchers to translate research workflows into scalable platform capabilities.


Preferred qualifications:: 
 Experience with Ray or other distributed AI orchestration frameworks.

 Experience with KAI, Slurm or other GPU scheduling technologies.

 Experience supporting reinforcement learning, simulation-driven training, robotics, or autonomy workloads.

 Experience deploying and optimizing AI models for edge hardware.

 Experience designing infrastructure for classified, sovereign, or air-gapped environments.

 Experience with observability technologies such as OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana.

 Experience contributing to or maintaining open-source infrastructure projects.


Why Join Us: The AI Factory is the foundation for how Shield AI develops and deploys autonomy. 

 As a Senior Staff Engineer, you will help build the reference architecture used internally by our engineering teams and delivered to customers building their own AI capabilities. Your work will directly impact how quickly researchers can iterate, how efficiently compute resources are utilized, and how AI systems move from experimentation to operational deployment. 

 This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of modern AI, distributed systems, Kubernetes, and defense, building a platform that enables the next generation of autonomy systems while leveraging the best of the open-source AI ecosystem.

 Investigate field-reported issues and drive root cause analysis across hardware, software, and integrated systems

 Analyze reliability and performance trends to identify systemic quality issues and improve product robustness

 Support validation, troubleshooting, and failure reproduction efforts for fielded systems

 Develop quality metrics, reporting, and tracking tools to improve visibility into field performance and defect trends

 Coordinate issue resolution across cross-functional teams while ensuring timely communication and closure




Required qualifications:: 

 5+ years of experience in quality engineering, field engineering, systems integration, manufacturing quality, or related technical roles

 Strong experience with root cause analysis, failure investigation, and corrective action implementation in complex hardware environments

 Ability to diagnose system-level issues across mechanical, electrical, and software interfaces

 Experience analyzing reliability data, defect trends, and operational performance metrics

 Strong communication and organizational skills with the ability to coordinate across engineering and operations teams

 Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in fast-paced development and operational environments




Preferred qualifications:: 

 Experience supporting aerospace, defense, robotics, or autonomous systems programs

 Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, or regulated engineering environments

 Experience with environmental testing, system validation, or field operations support

 Experience using data analysis and reporting tools such as Python, SQL, Jira, Power BI, or Tableau

This role supports engine integration, fuel systems, oil systems, pumps, and related propulsion hardware from development through production. 
The ideal candidate has deep experience with propulsion-related manufacturing processes, fluid systems integration, and production support for mission-critical hardware. 

What you'll do:: 

 Lead manufacturing engineering support for propulsion and fluid system assemblies 

 Develop and optimize manufacturing processes, tooling, work instructions, and production flows for: 

 Engines and propulsion systems 

 Fuel systems and fuel tanks 

 Oil and lubrication systems 

 Pumps and fluid control hardware 

 Aerospace vector and thrust systems 

 Partner with design engineering to improve manufacturability, reliability, testability, and producibility 

 Drive root cause investigations and corrective actions for propulsion manufacturing issues 

 Develop work instructions, quality standards, and inspection methods 

 Support supplier qualification, process validation, and production readiness reviews 

 Lead DFM/DFA reviews and transition new products into manufacturing 

 Support system integration, validation, and troubleshooting activities 

 Define manufacturing standards, process controls, and acceptance criteria 

 Support failure analysis and reliability improvement initiatives 

 Collaborate with production, quality, supply chain, and test engineering teams 

 Mentor junior manufacturing engineers 




Tools & skills:: 

 MES & QMS systems

 3DEXPERIENCE / Teamcenter (PLM) systems

 Supplier manufacturing processes

 5S/visual management

 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)




Required qualifications:: 

 7+ years of manufacturing engineering experience supporting propulsion or fluid systems 

 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing 

 Experience in prototype manufacturing in a startup or rapid-growth environment. 

 Experience with: 

 Engine assembly and integration 

 Fuel and oil systems 

 Precision fluid system manufacturing 

 Aerospace propulsion hardware 

 Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and adapt to changing priorities. 

 Knowledge of manufacturing process development and production scaling 

 Strong understanding of DFM/DFA principles 

 Experience with root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies 




Preferred qualifications:: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Aerospace or defense industry experience 

 Experience supporting turbine, piston, hybrid-electric, or UAV propulsion systems 

 Knowledge of pressure systems, leak testing, and fluid handling 

 Familiarity with lean manufacturing and production optimization 

 Experience with ERP/MES systems and manufacturing data analysis 

 Strong project management skills, including experience managing multiple priorities and deadlines 

 Knowledge of quality standards, such as AS9100 or ISO 9001 

 Proficiency in CAD software

Job Description:
At Shield AI, we’re building advanced autonomous aircraft that are redefining what is possible, and we are looking for a Staff Quality Engineer to help ensure our products meet the highest standards of performance, reliability, and safety. In this role, you will lead quality initiatives across the product lifecycle, driving improvements from early design and new product introduction through full-rate production.
 
You will be responsible for developing and maintaining robust quality systems in alignment with AS9100 standards, leading root cause investigations and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions. You will partner closely with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to identify risks, improve process capability, and ensure consistent product quality. Your work will include supporting NPI efforts, establishing control plans and inspection strategies, and using data-driven methods to monitor and improve manufacturing performance.

As a Staff Quality Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping quality strategy, mentoring team members, and influencing cross-functional decisions without direct authority. This is an opportunity to work hands on with next generation aerospace technology and contribute directly to the delivery of highly reliable autonomous systems that will define the future of aviation.

Required qualifications:: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)

 5+ years of experience in Quality, Manufacturing, or Process Engineering roles

 Demonstrated experience leading root cause analysis and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions (RCA/CAPA)

 Strong knowledge of quality systems and standards (AS9100 or similar)

 Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI) and scaling production in a manufacturing environment

 Proficiency in statistical analysis and process control methods (SPC, capability analysis, etc.)

 Proven ability to work cross-functionally and influence engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams


Preferred qualifications:: 
 Experience in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries

 ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Lean Six Sigma certification, or equivalent

 Knowledge of design for quality principles, including DFMEA, tolerance analysis, and design reviews

 Experience working with quality and manufacturing systems (QMS, MES, PLM) and data analysis tools

 Familiarity with advanced inspection or test methods (metrology, NDT, automated inspection, etc.)

existing_roles.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 DIRECTOR, STARLINK PRODUCTION (ASSEMBLY) 

 We are seeking a highly motivated and achievement-oriented leader to own Starlink Product Assembly Production in Bastrop, TX—scaling high-volume manufacturing to fuel global connectivity for millions. This includes oversight and responsibility for Assembly, Test, Manufacturing Engineering, Automation, and Maintenance across high-rate automated mechanical/pick & place, SMT/PCBA, and large electromechanical build production lines. This position plays a critical role in achieving rapid user expansion required for the success of the organization. Ideal candidates have a successful track record of scaling complex operations, leading 200+ person teams, and building cross-functional partnerships.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Oversee the strategic & tactical execution of Starlink Product Production

 Lead 250+ staff (multiple direct reports) across engineering and operations.

 Lead and mentor high-performing teams of manufacturing, process, and automation engineers to operationalize and continuously improve production.

 Implement a development program to enhance the capability of all team members while improving quality and reducing lead time & cost.

 Partner with Responsible Engineering teams to embed manufacturability into the design of new products and production lines.

 Ensure a strong focus is placed on safety and maintain an excellent safety record.

 Champion continuous improvement projects using appropriate metrics & data.

 Use quality metrics to continually improve the quality output of the operation.

 Manage resource levels to ensure optimum performance of the team.

 Monitor and communicate area status/readiness and risks to leadership.

 Monitor and maintain compliance with internal quality and customer contractual requirements.

 Foster a spirit of cooperation and collaboration within and between departments.

 Meet tight production schedules to achieve high-rate production, while adapting to changing priorities in a fast-moving environment.

 Think creatively and drive innovation; question the status quo, while following documentation and maintaining prescribed quality standards.

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in a STEM or engineering discipline OR 7+ years of production/manufacturing experience.

 5+ years of experience in production/manufacturing/operations.

 5+ years of experience in people leadership. 

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Experience managing large teams comprised of engineering and operations.

 Thorough knowledge of electronics manufacturing and test techniques.

 Experience monitoring cost and quality (ISO 9000, AS9100) standards.

 Experience developing and delivering continuous improvement projects within a production environment.

 Experience in fast-paced iterative design environments within the consumer electronics, mobile handset, medical devices, or automotive industries.

 Able to communicate complex concepts, problems, and solutions clearly and effectively to all levels within the organization.

 Demonstrated ability to act and execute in a scrappy, entrepreneurial manner against tight timelines and aggressive schedules.

 Strong desire to mentor and grow employees and manage out poor performers.

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 Willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed.

 Willing to travel as needed, up to 25%.

 ITAR REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here .  

 
 SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

 Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to  EEOCompliance@spacex.com .

 PRODUCTION DIRECTOR (STARSHIP) 

 SpaceX is revolutionizing the space industry by challenging what is possible and relentlessly pursuing continuous improvement to make life multiplanetary. The Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy booster form the most powerful launch system ever developed, designed to carry crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and beyond. As Director of Starship Production at Starbase, you will lead large-scale, multi-disciplinary production teams and complex manufacturing projects.

 This is a hands-on leadership role that requires diving deep into the unique engineering and production challenges of building flight hardware at unprecedented cadence and scale. You will lead some of the most passionate and capable technicians and engineers on the planet. By driving process excellence, optimizing production systems, and fostering a high-performance culture, you will make a lasting impact on humanity’s journey to space—turning ambitious goals into flight-ready vehicles.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Oversee the strategic and tactical execution of Starbase Production Operations such that manifest milestones are consistently achieved

 Manage overall staff and several direct reports

 Collaborate extensively with engineering leaders to ensure vehicle development meets all critical timelines and does not impact schedule to launch

 Meet tight production schedules to achieve high-rate production, while adapting to changing priorities in a fast moving environment

 Maintain productive relationships and often influence others outside of area of responsibility

 Lead and develop a high performing culture whereby people leadership is an essential responsibility

 Ensure a strong focus is placed on safety and maintain an excellent safety record

 Champion continuous improvement projects using appropriate metrics and data sources

 Foster a spirit of cooperation and collaboration within and between support departments

 Think creatively; question the status quo, while following documentation and maintaining prescribed quality standards

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in an engineering field or at least 8+ years of experience in a production/military/automotive environment

 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing/engineering leadership role

 2+ years of experience in a managerial role overseeing indirect reports

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Proven track record of building, motivating, mentoring, and coaching high performance manufacturing teams

 Technical project management experience

 Excellent technical expertise and judgement across multiple engineering disciplines permitting peer-level review of your team’s work product

 Creative problem solving that can bring multiple disciplines together

 Ability to assess risk and make development decisions without all available data

 Excellent verbal and written communication skills with direct experience negotiating integrated system trades between various stakeholders

 Experience working with cross-functional teams and external customers or vendors

 Highly detail oriented and passionate about advancing the commercial space industry

 Ability to work in a fast-paced, autonomously driven, and demanding start-up atmosphere

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

 Able to travel for short and extended trips as needed (up to 10% travel)

existing_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Power Plant (Starship)
existing_roles.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 SENIOR MANAGER 

 SpaceX is building and operating combined-cycle gas turbine power plants that must come online, stay online, and perform. This role owns the design and build of the full power plant: gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, and everything else that keeps the plant running at rated output, day after day. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Build, lead, and develop a multi-disciplinary power plant team spanning gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, controls, and commissioning

 Own the full lifecycle of gas turbine power generation assets — installation, commissioning, startup, operations, and long-term maintenance — and be accountable for plant availability, reliability, and performance

 Set technical direction and execution plans for commissioning, including combustion tuning, control system checkout, protective relay testing, and performance/reliability run verification

 Own root-cause analysis and corrective action for turbine trips, forced outages, and performance degradation; drive fixes that prevent recurrence and hold the team to a no-repeat standard

 Establish and continuously improve operating procedures, startup/shutdown sequences, and abnormal operating condition playbooks

 Serve as the primary technical and commercial interface with OEMs (GE, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan) on warranty issues, LTSA scope, outage planning, and technical issues

 Plan, staff, and execute major/minor inspections, hot gas path outages, and combustion inspections in line with OEM maintenance intervals; own outage cost, duration, and quality of return-to-service

 Drive turbine performance analysis (heat rate, capacity factor, degradation curves) to identify efficiency losses and convert findings into funded corrective action

 Coordinate across balance-of-plant teams (HRSG, steam turbine, cooling systems, water treatment) to deliver integrated plant performance, not siloed subsystem success

 Own the construction-to-operations handoff with EPC contractors; ensure a clean transition from construction to commercial operation

 Develop and own spare parts strategy, critical spares inventory, and maintenance budgets; manage spend against reliability and availability targets

 Hire, coach, and retain engineers and technicians; set performance standards and grow the next generation of plant leadership

 Represent the power plant organization to internal stakeholders (operations, grid interconnection, commercial, construction) and make timely field decisions under pressure

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 14+ years of experience working utility-scale gas turbines in commissioning, operations, maintenance, or plant engineering roles

 2+ years of project management experience leading operations

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES: 

 
 Working knowledge of combined-cycle plant systems: gas turbines, HRSGs, steam turbines, generators, and balance-of-plant equipment

 Experience reading and interpreting P&IDs, single-line diagrams, and turbine control logic

 Direct commissioning or operations leadership experience with GE 7/9HA, Siemens Energy SGT6/8-8000H, Mitsubishi M501/701JAC, or Doosan H-class turbines

 Experience with DCS/turbine control platforms (Mark VIe, SPPA-T3000, or equivalent)

 Familiarity with LTSA structures, OEM contract negotiation, and outage scope development

 Background in root-cause failure analysis (RCA/5-Why/Fishbone) for rotating equipment

 Experience with performance monitoring tools and heat balance modeling

 Exposure to grid interconnection requirements, PPA performance obligations, or capacity market rules

 Experience integrating power generation with co-located industrial or data center loads

 Proven ownership of plant or fleet reliability metrics (availability, forced outage rate, heat rate) and of the budgets that fund them

 Experience standing up a new plant, commissioning organization, or operations team from construction through commercial operation

 A bias toward action: comfortable making a call in the field without waiting for a committee

 Demonstrated ability to work under pressure during startup, outages, or unplanned events, with a sense of urgency and ownership over outcomes

 Experience using SOLIDWORKS, Siemens NX, or similar CAD software

 Knowledge of engineering standards and best practices such as ASME B31.3, ASME BPV Code Section VIII, and AFSPCMAN 91-710

 ITAR REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.  At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 We are seeking a dynamic Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering and Technology to oversee our aerospace component production processes. This pivotal role will lead teams in achieving operational excellence while collaborating with cross-functional departments to continuously enhance manufacturing operations. The ideal candidate will be results-driven, adept at resource management, and committed to maintaining high-quality standards in a fast-paced environment.
 
 We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 
 Position Specific Details: 
 Location: Space Coast, FL

 Lead and optimize manufacturing operations to ensure efficiency and quality.

 Support new product introductions and scale up production capabilities.

 Team Focus & Domain Expertise: 
 In this role you will lead and mentor a team of Manufacturing Engineers and Planners who are developing and supporting the design and fabrication of machined parts, advanced metal forming, and wire harnesses. This role will require you to demonstrate your ability to interact with the vehicle to proactively improve design for manufacturability, eliminate barriers and solve unforeseen technical problems.
 
 Minimum Qualifications: 
 5+ years of experience managing a team within a manufacturing or aerospace environment.

existing_roles.description:
Company Overview 
ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments. 
 Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community. 
 Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security. 
 ACS is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional operations in Alexandria, Virginia; Mountain View, California; and Huntsville, Alabama. For more information, visit allencontrolsystems.com . 
 
 Position Overview 
We're looking for a Director of Quality to build our quality function from the ground up — including our path toward ISO 9001 — and lead it for the long haul. This role sets the multi-year quality strategy while staying grounded in what's really happening on the floor, in the supply base, and with customers. Our hardware matters; defects here aren't abstract metrics. Our core philosophy is quality at the source: quality can't be inspected in after the fact, it has to be built right the first time. QA is the backstop, not the primary defense — an escape that reaches the customer is a production failure, not a QA failure.
We want a pragmatic leader who favors simple, practical problem-solving (5 Whys, direct observation) over paperwork-heavy processes, and who will build a genuine partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers to catch issues at the source rather than at receiving.

 What You'll Do: 

 Strategic & Long-Range Leadership 
• Own the long-range quality strategy, translating business goals into a multi-year plan for systems, staffing, and capability.
• Architect our Quality Management System — including our path toward ISO 9001 — from the ground up, building processes that are clear and simple, not just audit-ready.
• Own the audit calendar as the QMS matures, treating findings as strategic input, not a checkbox.
• Set and report quality KPIs (defect rates, first-pass yield, complaints, supplier performance); a data point is noise, a trend is a signal.
• Put every requirement, gate, and approval on trial — if no one can name who owns it and why it exists, that's the signal to cut it, not preserve it.

 Ground Truth & Root Cause 
• Get out onto the floor, into supplier facilities, and in front of customers regularly — not just working from what's reported up the chain.
• Personally lead or coach RCCA using practical, lightweight tools (5 Whys, direct observation) instead of heavy formal methodologies when they aren't warranted.
• Move with urgency: default to “why can't this be fixed today,” not “when can we fit this in.”

 Supply Chain & Supplier Quality 
• Build a close partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers, treating supplier quality as a shared mission.
• Drive supplier qualification, scorecards, and joint problem-solving to resolve issues at the source.
• Serve as the primary quality point of contact for DCMA surveillance, audits, and findings.

 Stakeholder Relationships 
• Partner especially closely with Engineering and Manufacturing — closing the loop between field/production issues and design decisions, and keeping quality and throughput goals aligned.
• Own key external customer relationships on quality matters, building credibility through transparency and follow-through.

 Team & Culture 
• Manage, mentor, and develop the quality team with a bias toward action and practical problem-solving.
• Keep the QMS lean — every process should exist because it supports a real decision, not because it looks good on paper.
• Own customer complaints and non-conformances through to true root cause and permanent corrective action.

 What You'll Need: 
• 8+ years in quality leadership, ideally in manufacturing, hardware, or defense/aerospace.
• Experience building or scaling a QMS; ISO 9001 experience strongly preferred (we are not yet certified — you'll help drive us there).
• A track record of practical, tool-light RCCA (5 Whys, direct observation) over heavyweight, paperwork-driven processes.
• Experience partnering closely with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers.
• Comfort operating at both strategic altitude and on the floor — this is a hands-on role, not a desk job.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to influence engineering, manufacturing, and executive leadership alike.
 What We Offer 
 Competitive salary

 ACS Equity Package

 Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

 Paid Time Off

 Allen Control Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer, providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment. Allen Control Systems prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

existing_roles.description:
Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future 
 Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.
 
Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.
 
Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.
 
If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.
 
 The Role: 
 The Senior Manager, Quality owns program quality end to end and leads the Quality Engineering team that supports it. You will build and lead a team of Quality Engineers across the program's process areas, owning requirements into our AS9100D quality management system, and be the single point of accountability for whether product is built to spec, on schedule, and with the objective quality evidence to prove it.
 
 What You'll Do 
 • Team leadership — build, lead, and develop the Quality Engineering team supporting the project across sheet metal, welding and forming, NDT, foundry and forging, machining, and additive manufacturing.
 • Staffing and coverage — close the open QE positions on the program, set priorities, and ensure every process area has quality coverage.
 • Development and standards — coach QEs, set consistent standards of practice, and grow special-process competency (welding, NDT) across the team.
 • Cross-functional partnership — represent quality with Build Engineering, Operations, and the program team, and serve as the escalation point for quality decisions on Nautilus.
 • Program quality for Nautilus — first-article inspection (AS9102), product qualification, and quality across the build from receipt to delivery.
 • Non-conformance and corrective action — control non-conforming material and customer escapes, drive root-cause and corrective action to closure, and own escape management for the program.
 • Supplier and receiving quality — flow requirements to suppliers, verify certifications and OQE at receipt, and build receiving capability for controlled material.
 • Audit readiness — prepare for and lead customer, and AS9100 audits for the program, and own the internal-audit posture that keeps it compliant.
 • Metrics and reporting — quality KPIs, escape trends, and program quality status to leadership.
 
 What We’re Looking For 
 • 8+ years in quality within defense, marine, nuclear, or aerospace manufacturing, including direct people-management of a quality team.
 • Proven command of AS9100 / ISO 9001 and hands-on experience integrating customer and regulatory requirements into a QMS.

 The Role 
 We're hiring our first Sr. Manager of Production Planning & Scheduling to own the factory side execution. Where our S&OP function decides where and whether we can build across the network, you own how and when it actually gets built on the floor. You'll own discrete operational scheduling, job sequencing and priority, and the daily/weekly rhythm that ensures on-time delivery (OTD) and sets the factory up for success.
 This role reports to our Operations leadership and drives a consistent scheduling methodology across the network, while partnering closely with each site General Manager on execution. Your scheduling and planning team members will support the sites day-to-day (dotted-line to the GM) while you own the standards, methodology, and rigor centrally.
 This is a builder and owner role. While the team is built out, you'll be hands-on developing the scheduling methodologies, communication rigor, and visual management that don't exist yet, and turning them into standard work. You'll be the person the floor, Program Management, and leadership rely on for a clear, credible answer to "what are we running, in what order, and are we going to hit the date?"
 You'll partner tightly with the S&OP function, translating network-level allocation and capacity plans into an executable factory schedule — and feeding real execution signal back up to highlight and drive capacity improvements.
 What You'll Do: 
 Own Production Scheduling & Execution 
 · Own discrete production scheduling and job sequencing across work centers to maximize on-time delivery and throughput.
 · Own work order release to the floor and control what work is released and when.
 · Set and manage priority and milestone dates, establish clear, transparent rules for what runs when, and make the trade-off calls when priorities conflict.
 · Own data integrity for schedules and dates in the system, and maintain and drive accurate MRP schedules so plans, priorities, and downstream commitments can be trusted.
 · Build the daily/weekly scheduling cadence and standard work that keeps the floor aligned, from shift-level execution to weekly look-ahead.
 · Translate S&OP network allocation and capacity plans into an executable, sequenced factory schedule.
 · Partner closely with the site General Manager to align on priorities, sequencing, and daily execution serving as the GM's right hand for turning the plan into on-time output.
 · Establish the system and cadence for tracking work order progress through the floor, monitors status against milestone dates, surfaces at risk jobs early, and drives rapid recovery on exceptions.
 Drive OTD & Factory Performance 
 Own on time delivery as a primary metric track it, root cause misses, and close the gaps.

 Ensure the factory is set up for success: materials, tooling, capacity, and priorities aligned ahead of the work, not discovered at the machine.

 Highlight and drive capacity improvements — surface constraints and bottlenecks from real execution data and partner with Operations and Engineering to resolve them.

 Feed execution signal (actual cycle times, constraints, attainment) back to S&OP to sharpen capacity models and sellable-capacity commitments.

 Build Methodology, Rigor & Visibility 
 Develop the scheduling methodologies and logic from the ground up, sequencing rules, buffering, prioritization frameworks and codify them as standard work applied consistently across sites.

 Establish communication rigor: the meeting cadence, escalation paths, and reporting that keep the floor, the GMs, and leadership on the same page.

 Build the visual management schedules, boards, dashboards, and status views that make factory status, priorities, and risks obvious at a glance.

 Establish key scheduling metrics: OTD, schedule adherence, past due, work center utilization, and cycle time performance.

 People Leadership 
 Lead, coach, and develop a team of production planners and schedulers as the function scales, including team members embedded at and dotted lined to the sites.

 Build organizational capability through talent development, standard work, training, and performance management.

 Foster a culture of accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement.

 · Deep understanding of production scheduling, sequencing, priority management, master scheduling, capacity/constraint analysis, and OTD drivers.

 Role Summary 
 The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering leads the technical arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside Build Engineering and partner directly with the Customer Programs team, owning the manufacturing scoping of new customer engagements: translating what a customer wants into what Hadrian will actually commit to and build.
 This role works directly with customers every day. For many of them, you and your team are the face of Hadrian engineering, so how you show up in the room matters as much as the technical answer. The work starts with discovery. Before anything is proposed, you and your team get inside the customer's operation: observing how work actually flows, mapping their processes and constraints, and interviewing the people closest to the problem until you understand what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for.
 From there, you shape a solution that maximizes what the customer gets out of the engagement and builds toward where Hadrian is headed. The craft is steering to the answer where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other: high impact, low effort, and built on what we already do well rather than new obligations we then have to invent our way out of.
 The intent behind housing this role in Build Engineering is clean accountability: your team scopes what we commit to, and Build Engineering delivers it. That means the commitments you shape have to be grounded in first-principles engineering judgment and a real understanding of the factory, not optimism. You evaluate and understand before you propose or promise.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Represent Hadrian with customers day to day: Own the technical relationship with customer engineering, program, and leadership teams. Run working sessions, present findings and recommendations, handle hard questions and pushback in the room, and follow up with clear, accurate written communication. Every interaction should leave the customer more confident in Hadrian.

 Discover before you design: Embed with customers to observe their operations, map processes, constraints, and pain points, and interview stakeholders from the shop floor to program leadership. Build a clear, evidence-based picture of the real need before any solution is on the table.

 Shape the solution: Fold what you learn into a solution that maximizes customer output and moves Hadrian toward what we are building. Hold an accurate picture of current capability and roadmap, and steer each engagement to the point where those two goals reinforce each other, favoring existing capabilities over new obligations.

 Partner with Customer Programs: Operate on a dotted line to Customer Programs as their forward deployed engineering arm, bringing technical judgment into every engagement from first conversation through commitment.

 Lead the forward deployed engineering team: Build, manage, and develop a technical team that engages directly with customers during new program scoping. Set the standard for how the team runs discovery, evaluates opportunities, and communicates with customers in a technical, credible, low-ego way.

 Scope new customer engagements: Own the manufacturing scoping of new engagements: review requirements, drawings, specifications, tolerances, materials, and volumes, and define a manufacturing solution that Hadrian can commit to with confidence.

 Evaluate before you promise: Bring a first-principles engineering mindset to every engagement. Understand the problem and the constraints before proposing or committing to a solution, so that what we sign up for is real and deliverable.

 Hand off cleanly to Build Engineering: Ensure every commitment is scoped so that the Build Engineering organization can deliver it: clear product definition, make-vs-buy posture, process capability requirements, and a manufacturing plan that stands up to execution.

 Drive leverage, not one-offs: Recognize recurring customer patterns and turn them into repeatable scoping approaches and reusable solution templates, so the function scales with the business instead of scaling headcount linearly.

 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field and 8+ years of manufacturing or manufacturing engineering experience, or 12+ years of that experience without a degree.

 3+ years managing technical teams (direct reports).

 Experience in a customer-facing technical role (e.g., applications, field or sales engineering, program engineering, or consulting), including presenting technical recommendations to customer engineering and program leadership.

 Proven ability to lead a technical team in a customer-facing capacity, translating between customer requirements and manufacturing reality.

 Demonstrated ability to run structured customer discovery (site visits, process mapping, stakeholder interviews) and turn it into a defined technical solution.

 Strong first-principles engineering judgment: able to evaluate and understand complex requirements before proposing or committing to solutions.

 Fluency reading and interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, and manufacturing process requirements.

 Experience scoping or defining manufacturing work: DFM, make-vs-buy, process planning, tooling strategy, or production launch.


 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience in aerospace, defense, maritime, or other high-complexity, high-mix manufacturing environments.

 Background spanning both a scaling/startup environment and a mature manufacturing organization.

 Exposure to precision machining, castings, forgings, sheet metal, or additive processes across metals and composites.

 Experience working alongside sales, program management, or commercial teams on new customer engagements.

 Exposure to manufacturing software and automation (MES/ERP, CAM automation, robotics, factory data systems), with a track record of feeding what you learn from customers back into product and automation roadmaps so those capabilities get built ahead of demand.

 A track record of building repeatable systems and templates rather than solving each problem from scratch.
