 Commissioning Chief Engineer, Marauder 
 Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing defense autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.
 Job Summary: 
 In this role you will be responsible for the commissioning and operation of the engine room and all associated machinery aboard a novel autonomous vessel. You will ensure that all marine systems — including but not limited to main propulsion, auxiliary machinery, fuel oil, lubrication, cooling, and associated environmental equipment — are properly tested and validated through structured commissioning processes and integrated with the vessel's autonomy and software control systems to support reliable manned, remote, and autonomous operation.
 The ideal candidate will possess strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities, along with the ability to develop procedures and processes in support of a novel commissioning environment. Have a strong grasp on vessel engineering systems with the ability to work independently on issues, including drafting and refining operational and technical documentation where none previously existed. A steadfast commitment to safety and adherence to maritime regulations is essential for ensuring the highest standards in vessel operations.
 Responsibilities 
 Lead and support commissioning activities for autonomous vessels, including system testing, validation, and troubleshooting prior to and during operation.

 Collaborate with autonomy and software engineering teams to verify integration between traditional machinery control systems and the vessel's autonomy stack across manned, remote, and autonomous operating modes

 Develop, write, and refine standard operating procedures, checklists, and technical documentation from scratch in the absence of established processes

Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, this role leads enterprise-wide technical investigations, drives engineering-based Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), and partners across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product, and Mission Operations to improve product reliability and operational performance.

This position applies deep engineering expertise to identify fundamental technical failure mechanisms, validate corrective actions through engineering analysis and testing, and eliminate systemic product and process risks.

The Staff Quality Engineer operates across multiple manufacturing sites and product lines, working with cross functional teams on design opportunities, manufacturing processes, and operational readiness while establishing best practices for technical problem solving across the enterprise.
 
 Technical Problem Solving
 Apply structured engineering methodologies to determine true physical, process, software, or systems root causes—not simply procedural gaps.

 Utilize advanced analytical tools including Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone, 5 Why, Statistical Analysis, Tolerance Stack Analysis, and FMEA.

 Validate corrective actions using engineering data, experimentation, testing, and verification.

 Drive permanent corrective actions that eliminate recurrence across products and manufacturing sites.

 
 Multi-Site Quality Leadership

 Standardize RCCA methodologies and engineering investigations across the enterprise.

 Coach site Quality Engineers on advanced engineering problem solving.

 Lead enterprise technical reviews for recurring issues and customer escapes.

 Support rapid problem escalation and recovery during production interruptions.

 
 Root Cause & Corrective Action (RCCA)
 Lead enterprise RCCA for manufacturing defects, supplier escapes, customer returns, field failures, and reliability issues.

 Ensure investigations identify technical root causes rather than symptoms.

 
 Manufacturing Quality Improvement
 Improve manufacturing capability through engineering analysis.

 Reduce defects through process optimization rather than increased inspection.

 Support New Product Introduction (NPI) Quality activities across multiple product lines.

 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration
 Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, Product Management, Mission Operations, and Executive Leadership.

 Present technical findings and recommendations to cross functional teams.

 
 Qualifications

 Extensive experience leading engineering-based RCCA.

existing_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing Engineering Automation & Controls
existing_roles.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders , soldiers in battlefield scenarios , and beyond .
 About the Role: 
 We are seeking a Head of Manufacturing Engineering to lead the development and scale-up of our manufacturing systems for high-volume small unmanned aircraft production. This leader will own the manufacturing engineering organization responsible for translating product designs into robust, automated, production-ready manufacturing systems capable of operating reliably at scale.
 A major focus of this role will be factory automation, controls engineering, equipment development, and manufacturing systems architecture. You will build and lead a multidisciplinary organization spanning manufacturing engineering, automation and controls, equipment engineering, process development, and production industrialization.
 The ideal candidate has experience scaling complex electromechanical products from early production into high-rate manufacturing, with a strong understanding of how automation, controls, data, equipment design, and process engineering come together to create a world-class production system.
 This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can establish the long-term manufacturing strategy while also driving execution on the factory floor.
 
 How You’ll Make an Impact: 
 Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Manufacturing Engineering organization supporting production from new product introduction through high-volume manufacturing.

 Define the manufacturing engineering strategy, technical roadmap, organizational structure, and capabilities required to support significant production growth.

 Partner closely with Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Test Engineering, and Product teams to ensure products are designed for manufacturability, automation, testability, and scale.

 Establish manufacturing standards, design reviews, equipment specifications, process qualification methodologies, and production-readiness criteria.

 Lead the architecture, development, deployment, and lifecycle management of automated manufacturing equipment and production systems.

 Build strong internal capabilities in controls engineering, PLC programming, industrial robotics, motion control, machine vision, industrial networking, sensors, servo systems, safety systems, and automated material handling.

 Establish controls and automation standards that enable equipment to be deployed, supported, replicated, and scaled rapidly across production.

 Develop strategies for balancing manual, semi-automated, and fully automated manufacturing based on production rate, process capability, economics, and product maturity.

 Establish disciplined equipment development processes including requirements definition, design reviews, FAT/SAT, commissioning, process validation, and production acceptance.

 Partner with external automation integrators and equipment suppliers while developing critical automation and controls capabilities internally.

 Build a highly instrumented manufacturing environment where equipment and processes generate actionable production data.

 Partner with software and data teams to connect manufacturing equipment with MES, traceability, quality, and factory data systems.

 Develop automated collection and analysis of process parameters, equipment states, cycle times, downtime, quality results, and genealogy.

 Use manufacturing data to identify process drift, predict failures, improve yield, and accelerate root-cause analysis.

 
 What Makes You a Good Fit: 
 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, automation engineering, controls engineering, equipment engineering, or related disciplines.

 5+ years of experience leading engineering organizations responsible for manufacturing systems or factory automation.

 Demonstrated experience scaling complex electromechanical products into high-volume production.

 Experience in aerospace, automotive, robotics, industrial automation, electronics, battery, semiconductor, or another highly engineered manufacturing environment; aerospace experience strongly preferred.

 Deep understanding of manufacturing automation and controls, including several of the following:
 PLC and industrial controls architectures

 Robotics and robotic cells

 Servo and motion-control systems

 Machine vision

 Industrial networking and communications

 Sensors and instrumentation

 Automated test and inspection

 Machine safety systems

 SCADA/HMI systems

 Manufacturing equipment software

 
 Experience developing custom production equipment from concept through production deployment.

 Experience developing capital equipment strategies and managing significant CapEx programs.

 Strong understanding of DFM/DFA and the ability to influence product architecture to enable manufacturing scale and automation.

 Experience operating in environments requiring rigorous configuration management, traceability, process control, and quality systems.

 Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and lead multidisciplinary technical organizations.

 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to move between factory-level strategy and detailed engineering problems.

 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related technical field.

 Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.

 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience scaling aerospace or similarly complex hardware from low-rate initial production to hundreds or thousands of units per month.

 Experience building an automation and controls engineering function from the ground up.

 Experience designing manufacturing systems for products combining mechanical assemblies, electronics, motors, sensors, batteries, composites, or other complex electromechanical technologies.

 Familiarity with aerospace manufacturing and quality frameworks such as AS9100.

 Experience with MES, equipment connectivity, manufacturing data infrastructure, and Industry 4.0 architectures.

 Experience with automated inspection, machine vision, robotic assembly, dispensing, fastening, material handling, or automated test systems.

 Experience developing standardized automation platforms that can be replicated across multiple production lines or factories.

 Experience working in fast-growth hardware organizations where product design and manufacturing systems evolve simultaneously.

 Master's degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent technical experience.

 
 Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $196,000 - $257,000*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria.

The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders , soldiers in battlefield scenarios , and beyond .
 About the Role 
 Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply, and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight. This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.
 
 Building on a head start 
 Skydio is the largest U.S.-based drone manufacturer, and we have treated secure supply chains as a strategic investment from the start. All of our current drone solutions, including X10, Dock for X10 and R10, are on the Blue UAS Cleared List. We have outgrown four U.S. manufacturing facilities in eight years. In April 2026 we committed $3.5 billion over five years to expand U.S. manufacturing through our SkyForge initiative, R&D and supply chain development. That includes a new U.S. factory five times the size of our current space and directing more than $1 billion to domestic suppliers. Through SkyForge, select suppliers will co-locate production with Skydio and work alongside our engineers, expanding and in some cases starting domestic manufacturing of critical parts. You will spearhead the SkyForge initiative and help decide where that investment goes and make sure it pays off: which components to onshore first, which suppliers to develop, and which capabilities to bring in-house.

 Section 232 tariffs and country-of-origin requirements

 Supply Chain and Manufacturing Strategy: Determine which capabilities and technologies we onshore, vertically integrate or partner on to build robust and compliant supply chains

 90 days: A complete risk baseline across products and regulations, separating hard blockers from cost problems, with named owners for every gap and a first readout to leadership.

 What you bring 
 Required 
 10+ years in supply chain, manufacturing operations, commodity management or operations strategy, including at least 3 in a regulated hardware environment where sourcing decisions carried legal or contractual consequences.

 Experience influencing component and supplier selection during design, through NPI, design reviews, or SPOR and approved vendor list (AVL) decisions.

 Credibility with both a sourcing organization and a factory. You can discuss capacity, tooling and yield as fluently as supplier qualification.

 Accountable ownership of a multi-tier country-of-origin, supplier compliance or trade compliance program.

 A make-versus-buy or vertical integration analysis you personally built and defended, including capex and ramp assumptions.

 A track record of turning technical findings into executive decisions, and of changing engineering or sourcing decisions you had no formal authority over.

 Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.

 Preferred 
 Working knowledge of NDAA §889/§848, country-of-origin and substantial-transformation analysis, Buy American domestic-content tests, or DFARS and FAR flow-downs

 Background in in-house manufacturing, UAS, aerospace and defense, defense electronics, or EMS and contract manufacturing

 Commodity experience in batteries and cells, motors and magnetics, imaging or thermal sensors, or PCB and PCBA

 Experience standing up a production line or bringing an outsourced process in-house

 Experience with a Blue UAS or Green UAS submission, or a DCMA or DCSA assessment

 Experience developing domestic or allied-country suppliers from scratch

existing_roles.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders , soldiers in battlefield scenarios , and beyond .
 About the Role: 
 The NPI Operations Engineering leader builds and leads the team responsible for making Skydio's next generation of autonomous robotics, including drones, docks and accessories, at our internal manufacturing facility in Hayward. You’ll deliver the process, manufacturing know-how and technology needed to build the most capable flying robots on the planet. The team combines Manufacturing Design Engineering and Supply Base Engineering into one organization that is 100% focused on new product development.
 You will own the manufacturability of every new product: assembly time, assembly yield and the processes, fixtures, equipment and supplier readiness needed to hit them. You and your team will engage with Product Engineering from early architecture, carry products through EVT, DVT and PVT, and hand them to Process Engineering for sustaining once they meet clear production-readiness criteria.
 This is a leadership role with significant scope to shape how Skydio develops hardware. You'll set the team's direction, hire and grow engineers, and be the single operations voice in product development. Sustaining engineering for products already in production sits with Process Engineering, so this team stays focused on getting new products right before they reach the line.
 
 How You’ll Make an Impact: 
 Own manufacturability of new products 
 Own the operations engineering development for NPI programs across supply chain and in-house manufacturing

 Drive design-for-manufacturing, assembly and serviceability (DFx) input from early architecture onward

 Set and commit to assembly time and assembly yield targets for each new product, and track them at every build

 Own operations sign-off at product development gates, and escalate manufacturability risks with clear trade-offs

 Use PFMEA, DFM reviews and prototype yield, quality and process data to align product design with manufacturing strategy

 Identify manufacturing risks early and drive mitigation plans to closure before production ramp

 Lead NPI execution through production readiness 
 Own the manufacturing plan for new products and major design changes, from prototype through PVT

 Define assembly flow, line layout, fixtures and equipment for new products, with labor, cost and capacity estimates that sharpen at each build

 Coordinate engineering, design and production validation builds with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Test and Quality

 Define production-readiness and handoff criteria, and lead manufacturing readiness reviews

 Develop and continuously improve Skydio's NPI process

 Transfer products to Process Engineering with complete documentation, released tooling, and yield and cycle time at target

 Develop processes, fixtures and assembly equipment 
 Own development and validation of assembly processes, including mechanical assembly, electronics integration, adhesive bonding, fastening, soldering and calibration

 Own design and qualification of assembly fixtures, error-proofing, and assembly equipment such as dispense systems and torque-controlled drivers

 Own the capital budget for new-product assembly fixtures and equipment. Capital for the running production line stays with Manufacturing

 Develop process specifications, control plans, component and assembly CTQs, inspections, inline tests, work instructions and manufacturing BOMs, all complete before handoff

 Use statistical process control (SPC), capability studies and structured experiments to establish robust process windows

 Develop core manufacturing technologies 
 Build a roadmap of core process technologies that future products depend on, such as waterproofing and ingress protection, conformal coatings, sealing and advanced bonding

 Partner with material suppliers, equipment vendors and technology partners to develop, qualify and industrialize these processes ahead of product need

 Serve as the technical owner for these technologies after production launch

 Lead supply base engineering for new products 
 Drive supplier selection, part qualification and supplier process readiness for new products

 Own NPI automation at the process level during development, and partner with the Factory Automation team for production handoff

 Work with suppliers on component DFM, process capability, capacity and quality before production launch

 Partner with Supply Chain and Quality on make-versus-buy decisions, supplier development and capital business cases

 Lead and build the team 
 Set the vision, strategy and execution plan for NPI Operations Engineering

 Lead, hire and develop a team of manufacturing design engineers and supply base engineers, acting as the team's lead technical expert and mentor

 Integrate MDE and SBE into one team with shared programs, goals and ways of working

 Set priorities and staffing across multiple concurrent programs and SKUs at different stages, working with leaders across the company to understand build targets and focus the team on hitting them

 Protect the team's focus on new products, with a clean handoff to Process Engineering for sustaining

 Build an inclusive, diverse, engaged and high-performing team through a mix of external hiring and developing internal talent, with regular coaching and growth opportunities

 Build a culture of technical rigor, ownership and close partnership with design engineering

 Collaboration 
 Work closely with Product Engineering leaders on airframes, propulsion, cameras, sensors, batteries, gimbals and payloads

 Align with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Test Engineering and Automation Engineering on capacity, equipment and handoff plans

 Communicate program status, risks and manufacturability trade-offs clearly to executive leadership
 

 What Makes You a Good Fit: 
 Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial or Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.

 10+ years of hands-on experience in manufacturing engineering, NPI or production engineering for complex electromechanical products, ideally including high-volume production.

 [4+] years leading engineering teams, including hiring and developing engineers [and managers].

 A track record of taking multiple complex hardware products from early development into high-quality production.

 Deep expertise in DFM/DFA and a history of influencing product design early, not only fixing problems at the build.

 Hands-on fixture design experience, and a strong understanding of factory lines, assembly flow and how to optimize them.

 SPC, Lean and Six Sigma experience.

 Experience working with suppliers on part qualification, process capability and production readiness.

 Strong data skills: you set yield, cycle-time and cost targets, measure them and use the data to drive decisions.

 Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, working collaboratively with people at every level, from technicians to executive leadership.

 Strong project management, analytical skills and attention to detail, with sound independent judgment on complex, broad-scope problems.

 Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with evolving products, and willingness to be on the floor during critical builds.

 Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.

 Nice to have 
 Experience with drones, aerospace, robotics, autonomous systems or consumer electronics.

 Experience developing waterproofing and ingress-protection solutions (IP-rated products), conformal coating, sealing or adhesive processes.

 Experience with PCBAs, cameras and optics, gimbals, inertial sensors, motors, batteries or composite structures.

 Experience working with contract manufacturers or managing NPI across in-house and outsourced production.

Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $229,500 - $302,500*. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. existing_roles.title: Director, Operations Program Management
existing_roles.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 Agility Robotics is scaling its operations — and the programs that enable that scale need to be led with rigor, depth, and autonomy. As Director, Operations Program Management, you will own two things simultaneously: a team of technical and non-technical program managers working across all of the operations and supply chain domains and a portfolio of high-complexity programs that span the full organization. 

 Reporting to the Sr. Director of Operations Program Management & Insights, you will bring the structure, judgment, and leadership presence to operate with minimal oversight. You set the standard for what great program management looks like on this team. 

 This is the right role for someone who leads from the front, develops the people around them, and can drive complex cross-functional programs to outcomes without being told how to get there. 

 About the Work 

 
 Lead and develop a team of dedicated program managers. Set clear expectations, coach toward growth, and hold yourself accountable to building a stronger team over time. 

 Establish and model PM best practices across the team. You are both the standard-setter and the coach. 

 Own, through your and the team’s efforts, a portfolio of complex programs that require a high degree of structure, judgment, and organizational reach. Act as a player-coach on the team’s broader portfolio — holding your own programs while helping your direct reports navigate blockers and deliver against theirs. 

 Translate complex, multi-org work into clear progress narratives for executive audiences. You know what leadership needs to see and how to present it. 

 Identify risks, stalled decisions, and at-risk dependencies before they become problems.  

 Other duties as assigned. 

 
 About You 

 
 10+ years in leadership roles, with a proven track record in Program Management. 

 Exceptional ability to translate complex concepts into clear messages for diverse audiences. 

 Build and mentor a diverse and growing team of technical and non-technical Program Managers. 

 Strong data-driven decision-making skills to manage a complex portfolio of initiatives across a range of departments. 

 Operate with a high degree of autonomy defining the path for you and the team. 

 Deep understanding of how manufacturing and operations environments work — with 7+ years of experience driving programs in this space. 

 Comfort working in organizations without mature systems, clean data, or clear processes. 

 
 Bonus Points 

 
 Prior experience managing or developing a team of program managers. 

 Background in high-growth hardware, automation, or robotics environments. 

 Experience designing or overhauling operational processes at scale — service operations, order fulfillment, or manufacturing workflows. 

 
 
  

 Location 

 
 This is a hybrid position based out of our Salem office.

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $149,000 — $193,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

existing_roles.title: Director, Product Quality
existing_roles.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 We are looking for a hands-on, high-impact Director, Product Quality  to lead our Field Quality and Failure Analysis engineering teams. In this role, you will hold ultimate accountability for overall field quality, reliability performance, and fleet health across all deployed commercial products. 

 You are a seasoned practitioner of rigorous problem-solving methodologies (8D, 5-Why, DMAIC) with a proven track record of diving deep into complex electromechanical, hardware, and firmware failures. You will bridge the gap between field service operations, customer sites, supplier quality, and internal product design teams to ensure field issues are contained rapidly, root-caused definitively, and prevented permanently. 

 About the Work 

 
 Own Field Quality & Fleet Health: Establish, monitor, and report on key field quality metrics (e.g., MTBI, MTTF, ARR, issue escape rates, service ticket turnaround time) for all shipping products and customer deployments. 

 Lead Failure Analysis (FA) & CAPA: Lead and grow a dedicated team of Failure Analysis Engineers. Drive rigorous Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for field returns, hardware bugs, and system-level failures. 

 Field Containment & Rapid Response: Establish immediate containment protocols for critical field escalations, safety events, and unexpected fleet-wide failure trends to minimize customer downtime. 

 Cross-Functional Feedback Loop: Serve as the critical bridge between Field Operations, Customer Success, Hardware Engineering, Software/Firmware, and Supplier Quality. Drive design-for-reliability (DFR) feedback directly into next-generation product engineering. 

 Manage Closed-Loop Quality Systems: Implement and maintain robust Closed-Loop Corrective Action (CAPA) tracking across multi-site field deployments and repair depots. 

 Executive Communication & Governance: Host regular Field Quality Reviews with leadership, presenting objective data, failure Pareto analyses, root-cause findings, and measurable CAPA progress. 

 
 About You 

 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. 

 Experience: 10+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Field Quality, or Reliability Engineering within high-complexity hardware industries (Robotics, Automotive/EV, Aerospace, Autonomous Systems, or Complex Industrial Equipment). 

 Leadership: 5+ years of direct people management experience leading technical engineering teams (FA, Quality, or Sustaining Engineering). 

 Hands-on Expertise: Deep, practical experience executing physical failure analysis on electromechanical systems (actuators, harnesses, sensors, PCBAs, battery management systems, and precision mechanical linkages). 

 Methodologies: Certified or expert practitioner in structured root cause analysis tools (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree Analysis, FMEA, Gauge R&R). 

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Advanced Degree: Master’s degree in Engineering Management or an Engineering discipline. 

 Certifications: Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. 

 Domain Experience: Experience managing field reliability for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robotics, or safety-critical industrial equipment. 

 Systems Exposure: Familiarity firmware diagnostic tools, and telemetry data analytics for remote fleet diagnostics. 

 
 Work Environment & Travel 

 
 Position is based out of our Salem, OR facility with regular access to testing labs, service centers, and assembly lines. 

 Occasional travel (up to 20%) to customer sites, field test locations, or primary suppliers may be required to investigate critical quality escapes. 

 
 
 Location

existing_roles.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 We are seeking an experienced Staff Manufacturing Quality Engineer to lead factory quality engineering across our final assembly, sub-assembly, and testing operations. In this role, you will hold technical ownership of line quality, process capability, and quality gate containment at our manufacturing facilities. You will partner cross-functionally with Manufacturing Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing, NPI, Supply Chain, and Design Engineering to establish rigorous process controls, qualify production lines, drive defect prevention, and ensure zero-escape assembly for mission-critical electromechanical systems. 

 About the Work 

 
 Own Factory Quality & Yield Performance: Establish, monitor, and drive continuous improvement across key manufacturing quality metrics—including First Time Quality (FTQ) First Pass Yield (FPY), Scrap & Rework Rates, and End-of-Line (EOL) failure escape rates across sub-assembly and final integration lines. 

 Drive Process Characterization & Statistical Control: Design and execute Measurement System Analysis (Gage R&R), Process Capability studies (Cp/Cpk), and Statistical Process Control (SPC) charting on critical-to-quality (CTQ) parameters, such as automated torque fastening, press-fits, PCBA flashing, and joint calibration. 

 Champion PFMEA & Control Plans: Develop, maintain, and rigorously update Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA) and manufacturing Quality Control Plans (QCP). Ensure lessons learned from field returns (CAPA/RMA) and NPI prototypes are proactively mitigated in line architecture. 

 Own Line 8D & Root Cause Problem Solving: Lead cross-functional problem-solving initiatives using 8D, DMAIC, 5-Why, and Fishbone methodologies for chronic manufacturing defects, line stops, and assembly quality escapes, driving verified corrective and preventive actions. 

 NPI to Production Quality Transition: Partner with NPI and Manufacturing Engineering during build phases (EVT/DVT/PVT) to audit assembly lines, validate line tooling/fixtures, sign off on quality gates, and certify line readiness for commercial rate ramp. 

 Standardize Quality Work Instructions & Inspection: Define and implement standardized incoming/in-process inspection criteria, quality verification fixtures, Go/No-Go tooling, and assembly quality checklists across workstations. 

 Executive Quality Reviews & Pareto Analytics: Analyze factory defect trends to publish regular quality Pareto analyses, root-cause summaries, and corrective action status updates to operations and engineering leadership. 

 
 About You 

 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial & Systems Engineering, Mechatronics, or equivalent technical degree. 

 Experience: 8+ years of hands-on Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, or Advanced Manufacturing experience supporting high-complexity, low-to-mid volume electromechanical systems (Robotics, Automotive/EV, Aerospace, Industrial Automation, or Medical Devices). 

 Process & Tooling Expertise: Proven expertise implementing quality controls for complex electro-mechanical assemblies, high-torque robotic actuators, precision gearboxes, structural bonded assemblies, wire harnesses, and PCBA/box-build integration. 

 Statistical & Quality Engineering Toolkit: Advanced practitioner in SPC, Gage R&R, Cp/Cpk analysis, PFMEA, Control Plans, IQ/OQ/PQ, and structured problem-solving methodologies (8D, DMAIC, 5-Why, Ishikawa, FTA). 

 Factory Systems Exposure: Direct experience working within Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platforms for quality gate enforcement and traceability. 

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Certified Quality Engineer (ASQ-CQE), Six Sigma Black Belt (SSBB), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA). 

 Experience with functional testing, End-of-Line (EOL) dyno/burn-in testing, and automated optical/laser measurement systems (CMM, Keyence, 3D profiling). 

 Familiarity with industrial automation and functional safety standards (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, ISO 13849). 

 Direct experience ramping automated or semi-automated production lines from prototype to volume manufacturing. 

 
 Work Environment & Travel 

 
 Based full-time on-site at our manufacturing facility in Salem, OR, with daily presence on the assembly floor, quality inspection areas, and test bays. 

 Occasional travel (up to 15%) to regional contract manufacturers, key sub-tier component suppliers, or our Fremont, CA engineering center. 

 
 
 Location  

 
 This is an onsite position at our Salem office.

existing_roles.description:
About Mach Industries 

 Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.

 Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.

 The Role 

 Mach Industries is seeking a Principal Manufacturing Engineer, Energetics to lead the development and industrialization of manufacturing systems for solid rocket motors (SRMs), pyrotechnics, and energetic products.

 This role will have end-to-end technical ownership of energetic manufacturing capability, from early manufacturing concepts and process architecture through facility buildout, equipment integration, commissioning, qualification, and production launch.

 You will define how energetic products are manufactured at scale: translating product and process requirements into manufacturing cells, production lines, hazardous-process facilities, equipment specifications, controls architectures, material flows, and commissioning plans.

 This is a highly cross-functional role requiring coordination across product engineering, manufacturing, automation, facilities, EHS, quality, operations, external A/E firms, equipment OEMs, and systems integrators.

 The ideal candidate has personally taken complex manufacturing systems from concept through production and is comfortable operating as the technical DRI for large, multidisciplinary capital projects.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Manufacturing System & Line Design 

 
 Own the manufacturing architecture for solid rocket motor, pyrotechnic, and other energetic production lines from raw material receipt through finished-product acceptance.

 Translate product requirements and production targets into manufacturing processes, equipment requirements, cycle times, staffing models, material flows, and factory layouts.

 Develop process flows, equipment concepts, line balancing, capacity models, manufacturing requirements, and capital equipment roadmaps.

 Establish equipment boundaries, interfaces, utilities, controls requirements, inspection strategy, and material-handling concepts.

 Lead design reviews including process, equipment, layout, automation, operability, maintainability, and production-readiness reviews.

 Identify manufacturing bottlenecks and develop scalable production architectures capable of supporting significant rate increases.

 Drive Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) feedback into product development.

 
 Energetics Process Industrialization 

 
 Industrialize manufacturing processes associated with solid rocket motors and pyrotechnic products, including energetic material preparation, mixing, casting/dispensing, curing, machining, assembly, inspection, testing, and material handling.

 Translate development processes into robust, repeatable production processes with defined operating windows and acceptance criteria.

 Develop process specifications, manufacturing requirements, equipment URS documents, control plans, and qualification strategies.

 Partner with EHS and process safety teams to incorporate energetic-material hazards into equipment and process design.

 Drive reductions in operator exposure and manual handling through appropriate automation, remote operation, process isolation, and engineered controls.

 
 Facility & Infrastructure Buildout 

 
 Serve as the manufacturing technical owner for new energetic production facilities and major facility expansions.

 Translate manufacturing processes into facility requirements including equipment layouts, utilities, hazardous-area requirements, material flows, personnel flows, storage requirements, and operational constraints.

 Work directly with architects, A/E firms, general contractors, EHS, authorities having jurisdiction, and equipment integrators throughout facility design and construction.

 Participate in concept design, basis-of-design development, FEED, detailed design, construction, installation, and startup.

 Ensure facility design supports production throughput, equipment maintainability, future expansion, safe operations, and efficient material movement.

 Own manufacturing requirements and interfaces between the facility, process equipment, automation systems, utilities, and production operations.

 
 Capital Equipment & Integration 

 
 Develop technical specifications and requirements for custom and off-the-shelf manufacturing equipment.

 Lead equipment vendor and systems-integrator selection from technical evaluation through execution.

 Own technical execution of major manufacturing equipment programs including design reviews, fabrication, integration, installation, and acceptance.

 Work with automation engineers and integrators to define controls, robotics, machine vision, data acquisition, traceability, and manufacturing software requirements.

 Review and approve equipment designs for process capability, safety, serviceability, controls architecture, and production readiness.

 Manage technical interfaces across multiple equipment suppliers and integrators to ensure individual systems function as a complete manufacturing line.

 
 Commissioning & Production Launch 

 
 Own manufacturing equipment commissioning and line startup from installation through production release.

 Develop and execute equipment acceptance and commissioning strategies including FAT, SAT, commissioning, process qualification, and production-readiness activities.

 Lead equipment debugging, process characterization, capability studies, and production trials.

 Establish equipment and process acceptance criteria and drive closure of technical issues identified during commissioning.

 Partner with Quality to establish inspection strategies, process controls, traceability, and manufacturing acceptance criteria.

 Drive production ramp by identifying and eliminating constraints related to equipment reliability, cycle time, yield, scrap, ergonomics, and process capability.

 Transition manufacturing systems to site operations and maintenance teams with appropriate documentation, training, spare-parts strategies, and sustainment plans.

 
 Technical Leadership 

 
 Act as a senior technical authority for energetic manufacturing systems across Mach Industries.

 Lead multidisciplinary technical decisions spanning manufacturing, automation, facilities, process safety, quality, and operations.

 Develop manufacturing standards and reusable architectures for future energetic production facilities.

 Mentor manufacturing and automation engineers and raise the technical standard for capital equipment execution across the organization.

 Independently identify technical and program risks and drive them to resolution.

 Communicate manufacturing strategy, technical tradeoffs, capital requirements, schedule risks, and execution status to engineering and company leadership.

 
 Required Qualifications  

 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

 10+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, industrialization, factory engineering, or capital equipment development.

 Demonstrated ownership of complex manufacturing equipment or production lines from concept through installation, commissioning, and production.

 Experience developing manufacturing processes and translating them into equipment and facility requirements.

 Experience specifying, procuring, integrating, and commissioning capital equipment.

 Experience working with equipment OEMs, systems integrators, construction teams, and/or A/E firms.

 Strong understanding of manufacturing fundamentals including process capability, line balancing, equipment reliability, yield, throughput, and production ramp.

 Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical programs across multiple engineering disciplines with limited oversight.

 
 Preferred Qualifications  

 
 Direct experience designing, building, commissioning, or operating solid rocket motor, propellant, pyrotechnic, ammunition, warhead, or other energetic-material manufacturing facilities.

 Experience with energetic processes such as material preparation, mixing, casting, dispensing, curing, machining, assembly, inspection, and testing.

 Experience taking an energetic manufacturing process from development or pilot scale into rate production.

 Experience with hazardous-process facility design and manufacturing equipment intended for explosive or energetic environments.

 Working knowledge of applicable explosives, fire protection, electrical, process safety, and DoD energetic-manufacturing requirements.

 Experience working with A/E and EPC organizations on greenfield or brownfield manufacturing facility projects.

 Experience developing equipment URS documents, RFQs/RFPs, statements of work, acceptance criteria, and capital project specifications.

 Experience executing FAT, SAT, commissioning, process qualification, and production acceptance.

 Experience with automated manufacturing equipment, PLC-controlled systems, robotics, machine vision, and manufacturing data systems.

 Experience building production systems within aerospace, defense, propulsion, munitions, automotive, semiconductor, chemical processing, or similarly demanding manufacturing environments.

 
 Additional Requirements 

 
 
 Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed

 


 
 ITAR Requirements 

 To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR  here .  


 Principal
 $180,000 — $220,000 USD 


 At Mach, we believe that compensation is more than just a paycheck. It's a comprehensive package designed to reward the time, skills, and expertise you bring to our team. We are committed to offering competitive compensation that is equitable, transparent, and aligned with market trends.

 Key Elements of Our Compensation Philosophy:

 
 Competitive Salaries : We continuously research market rates to ensure our salaries are competitive with those in our industry and geographic location.

 Performance-Based Incentives : Our bonus structure is tied to both individual and company performance, creating a win-win scenario that motivates our team members to excel.

 Equity Participation : We offer stock options or equity to employees, ensuring that you share in the success and growth of the company.

 Benefit Packages : Our benefits include healthcare, dental and vision plans, retirement savings, and paid time off, because we understand that your well-being extends beyond the office.

 Professional Development : We allocate funds for continuing education, training, and career growth.

 Transparency : We are committed to openness about our compensation tiers and how decisions are made, ensuring trust and mutual respect.

 
 By joining Mach, you’re not just accepting a job—you’re becoming a key part of a team that values your contributions and invests in your growth. Together, we aim to create a rewarding environment that sets the stage for long-term success.

 Data Privacy 
To view Mach Industries candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://machindustries.com/privacy-policy .

 Disclosures 

 This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).  Please note that any offer for employment may be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations without sponsorship for an export license.

 Mach participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offers may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and training, critical skills, and business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in most offers and are considered part of Mach’s total compensation package. Mach offers benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans, and opportunities for professional development.

 Mach is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, Veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law, including those with a criminal history, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws. If you’d like to defend the American way of life, please reach out!

existing_roles.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

 OUR MISSION 

 True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

 OUR VALUES 

 
 Be the offset.   We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

 What would it take?  We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

 It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

 
 BENEFITS & PERKS *

 
 Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

 Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

 Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

 And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

 Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

 
 *Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

 YOUR MISSION 

 We are looking for an operations leader to take ownership of the everyday workplace operations at True Anomaly. From office management to culinary, janitorial to groundskeeping to beyond, you'll lead the teams and vendors that keep our workplaces running at a high standard. You own the full OPEX picture for our workplaces — managing to budget, forecasting with rigor, and always bringing cost-saving options to the table. You think in partnerships: working hand-in-hand with Real Estate to draw the line between Landlord scope and ours and with Development Planners to set long-term standards that drive operational efficiency downstream. You're a people leader at heart, a sharp cross-functional partner, and you'll flex to support services in our production areas when the mission calls for it. You take immense pride in your craft, and that pride shows up everywhere — in workplaces that run well, employees who feel taken care of, and an operations function that scales like a well-oiled machine.

 RESPONSIBILITIES 

 Lead and develop operations teams across multiple workplaces to support ongoing day-to-day needs, including office management, culinary/snacks, janitorial, groundskeeping, and related services. Define and own third-party vendor strategy across all service categories, ensuring consistent quality, reliability, and cost-effectiveness across the portfolio. Own the full OPEX budget for our workplaces, reporting out on forecast vs. budget regularly and surfacing cost-saving options. Partner hand-in-hand with the Real Estate team to define what work scope is the Landlord's responsibility versus ours. Partner hand-in-hand with Development Planners to develop long-term standards that support operational efficiencies downstream. Build scalable operations standards and processes that support growth into additional sites while maintaining a strong employee experience across all spaces. Support services within production areas as needed. Serve as a people leader and cross-functional partner inside and outside Facilities.

 QUALIFICATIONS 

 Required 

 
 7+ years of experience in workplace operations

 People management experience, including developing and growing teams

 Proven ability to own and manage a full OPEX budget, including forecasting and cost-saving identification

 Proven ability to define and manage third-party vendor strategy across multiple service categories

 Experience partnering with real estate on lease scope (Landlord vs. tenant responsibilities)

 Demonstrated ability to build scalable operations standards and processes

 Track record of delivering a strong employee experience across multiple sites

 Experience scaling a workplace operations function into new sites in a high-growth environment

 Familiarity with office management, culinary, janitorial, and groundskeeping service categories

 
 Nice to Have 

 
 Experience supporting secure environments

 Experience supporting services within production or manufacturing areas

 
 OTHER 

 
 Work Location - This position will be onsite 4 to 5 days per week at our Long Beach, CA facility

 
 COMPENSATION 

 
 Base Salary: $145,000-$210,000

 Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

 
 Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education and experience. 
 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

existing_roles.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here. 
 

 
Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.  

 

 Role Overview 

 The Senior Director, Quality is the senior quality leader for Ursa Major. This leader is accountable for product quality, quality compliance, and the effectiveness of the Quality Management System across all sites and product lines, including solid rocket motors, hypersonic propulsion, in-space propulsion, and avionics. Reporting to the Chief Safety and Risk Officer, the Sr. Director serves as the company’s senior quality representative to DCMA, government customers, and prime contractors. They will build the program and customer-facing quality capability Ursa Major needs as it scales from development into rate production and operates as a public company.

 This role leads the full quality organization, including quality control, inspection, metrology and calibration, quality systems, and product quality engineering, with full authority to shape its structure as the business grows. The ideal candidate knows what prime-level quality looks like and how to deliver it at startup speed, scaling rigor to risk rather than adding bureaucracy. This is a senior leadership role, but it is also a hands-on one: we expect this leader to roll up their sleeves, lead from the front, and work in the trenches alongside the team as we scale.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Quality Leadership & Strategy 

 
 Own Ursa Major’s quality strategy, objectives, budget, and organization, structuring and developing the quality team to support growth across all product lines and sites.

 Build a culture of quality where every function owns quality and builds it into design, sourcing, manufacturing, and delivery.

 Match quality rigor to program maturity: move at the speed development programs require while meeting the full expectations of mature defense and prime customer programs.

 
 Government & Prime Customer Quality 

 
 Serve as Ursa Major’s senior quality representative to DCMA, government customers, prime contractors, and certification bodies, building trust-based relationships with DCMA quality assurance representatives and customer quality organizations.

 Lead quality across Ursa Major’s business models: all-up-round deliveries directly to the U.S. government, SRM and propulsion deliveries as a supplier to defense primes, and in-space propulsion systems for satellite and spacecraft customers.

 Build an organization capable of reviewing proposals and contracts for quality requirements, including FAR/DFARS quality clauses and customer-specific requirements, and ensure they flow down and implemented across design, purchasing, manufacturing, inspection, and delivery.

 Own government source inspection, product acceptance, and customer audit readiness, including WAWF acceptance, government first article approval, and witnessed lot acceptance testing.

 Partner with material control to 3nsure effective control of government-furnished property and material under FAR 52.245-1, and support DCMA property management system reviews in partnership with Supply Chain and Contracts.

 Lead the company’s response to customer corrective action requests, audit findings, and quality escapes.

 
 Program Quality 

 
 Build Ursa Major’s program quality function, providing dedicated quality ownership for major programs and customers from contract award through delivery.

 Own contractual quality deliverables and commitments, including first article inspection reports, acceptance data packages, certificates of conformance, as-built records, and customer witness and hold points, and represent quality in program reviews and customer meetings.

 
 Quality Systems & Product Quality 

 
 Own the AS9100 Quality Management System and scale it across sites and product lines, including certification and audits, management review, nonconformance and Material Review Board, corrective action, and Nadcap accreditation of special processes where customers require it.

 Maintain effective controls for configuration, traceability, quality records, foreign object prevention, and counterfeit parts prevention, including GIDEP reporting.

 Partner with Engineering and Mission Assurance on design reviews, qualification, first article, and production readiness, and support a disciplined production rate ramp across solid rocket motors, hydrazine satellite propulsion systems, and potential future liquid-engine all-up rounds.

 In partnership with Safety, ensure quality controls fit energetics manufacturing, including propellant processing, cast-cure operations, and lot control and traceability of energetic materials.

 Ensure quality coverage for avionics and electronics, including electronics assembly workmanship and software and firmware quality, developing the team expertise needed as the avionics business grows.

 Shape supplier quality through influence rather than ownership: partner with Procurement, which owns supplier engineering, to set supplier quality requirements and flowdowns, weigh in on the selection and approval of critical suppliers, and drive resolution of supplier escapes.

 
 Authority & Public Company Governance 

 
 Hold authority to stop production, testing, acceptance, or shipment when product conformity, safety, or contractual compliance may be compromised, with an independent escalation path to the CEO and Business Unit President.

 Lead cost of poor quality reduction and continuous improvement: partner with Finance to accurately capture scrap, rework, and warranty costs in line with public company financial controls and use that data to drive measurable improvements.

 Other duties as assigned.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.

 10+ years of progressive quality experience in aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated manufacturing, including 5+ years in senior quality leadership building, scaling, and leading quality organizations.

 Direct, hands-on experience working with DCMA, including quality surveillance, government source inspection, and corrective action requests.

 Direct experience serving U.S. government and prime contractor customers, including contract quality requirements, FAR/DFARS quality clauses, requirement flowdowns, and customer audits.

 Demonstrated experience leading and sustaining an AS9100-certified Quality Management System.

 Experience leading quality through the transition from development into production and rate ramp.

 Track record of right-sizing quality rigor to risk, maintaining compliance and product integrity without slowing execution.

 Proven ability to build and sustain a strong culture of quality, where ownership of quality extends well beyond the quality organization.

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Experience with solid rocket motors, energetic materials, propellant processing, munitions, or tactical propulsion (strongly preferred).

 Public company experience (strongly preferred), including board-level reporting or supporting public company internal controls; experience through an IPO is a plus.

 Experience in both a traditional prime and a startup or non-traditional defense environment.

 Familiarity with avionics and electronics quality, such as electronics workmanship standards (IPC J-STD-001, IPC-A-610), ESD control, and software and firmware quality assurance.

 Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.

 ASQ CMQ/OE, CQE, or CQA certification, or AS9100 lead auditor experience.

 
 Working Conditions / Physical Demands 

 
 Work performed in office, laboratory, and manufacturing environments, including hazardous and energetic operations areas that require personal protective equipment and adherence to explosives safety and site security protocols.

 Ability to sit or stand for extended periods and work on a computer for prolonged durations.

 Occasionally required to lift up to 25 pounds.

 Ability to travel up to 25% to Ursa Major sites, customers, suppliers, and government facilities.

 
 

  

 Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $225,000 - $275,000, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t  quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

existing_roles.title: VP of Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q)
existing_roles.description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life. 


The VP, Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q) holds the independent oversight authority that ensures every spacecraft is safe, reliable, and qualified before it launches. This role is structurally independent of all other VP organizations - the authority to halt work, reject deliverables, and withhold qualification sign-off cannot be overridden by any VP. Only the CTO can override an MA&Q determination, and that override is documented with the MA&Q position on record regardless of outcome.
 
Independence is the defining feature of this role. MA&Q does not build hardware, does not own schedule, and does not report to any VP who does. This structural separation is deliberate - quality and safety decisions must never be compromised by production pressure, schedule urgency, or cost targets.
 
The VP, MA&Q must be willing to halt a production line, delay a gate review, or withhold qualification sign-off when the evidence demands it - and hold that position under pressure from peers and the CTO alike.

What you’ll be doing:: 
 Mission Assurance 

 
 Own the FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification -zero unmitigated single-point failures is a CDR entry criterion 

 Chair the Failure Review Board (FRB) -convene, lead root cause investigation, assess extent of condition, and close with verified corrective action 

 Define mission success criteria and own fault tree analysis 


 Safety 

 
 Implement and own the system safety program per MIL-STD-882 or program-equivalent standard 

 Lead hazard analysis (PHA, SHA) and maintain the hazard tracking log through every gate 

 Manage propulsion, battery, high-voltage, and deployment safety; provide range safety interface for launch operations 


 Quality Assurance 

 
 Exercise independent inspection authority across all program phases 

 Hold sole NCR disposition authority -Use-As-Is and Repair require MA&Q concurrence regardless of phase 

 Enforce workmanship standards per IPC-A-610 Class 3; conduct process audits and first article inspections 

 Issue Standing Disposition Authorizations (SDAs) for recurring Tier 2/3 NCRs; Tier 1 Critical NCRs trigger CTO notification within 4 hours 


 Reliability Engineering 

 
 Own quantitative reliability model per MIL-HDBK-217 or equivalent; track MTBF/MTTR targets against the constellation availability model 

 Lead reliability growth tracking, redundancy analysis, and reliability predictions correlated with test data at QR 


 Parts Engineering & Radiation 

 
 Maintain the Preferred Parts List (PPL) - sole authority to add or remove parts; no part may fly without PPL approval 

 Enforce derating compliance at CDR and manage lot acceptance testing 

 Specify the mission radiation environment (TID, SEE, displacement damage) and track radiation margins for all flight parts 


 Configuration Management 

 
 Chair the production CCB and administer the ECO/ECN process 

 Maintain as-built configuration records from the MES; execute FCA and PCA before Phase Close Gate 

 Provide as-built conformance report to the CTO 


 

What you bring to this role:: 
 
 15+ years of progressive mission assurance, quality engineering, or reliability engineering on flight programs; at least one spacecraft program carried from system requirements through on-orbit operations 

 Demonstrated record of exercising halt/reject authority or withholding qualification sign-off against schedule and cost pressure you must describe a specific instance. This is the most important qualification for the role 

 Direct accountability for a flight program's FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification, including enforcing zero-unmitigated-SPOF at CDR 

 Experience designing, implementing, and running a tiered NCR classification and disposition system at production rate, including Use-As-Is and Repair disposition authority 

 Direct experience chairing or co-chairing a spacecraft Qualification Review and making the independent go/no-go determination 

 Familiarity with PPL management, derating analysis, lot acceptance testing, and radiation qualification requirements (TID, SEE) 

 Demonstrated record of building multi-discipline assurance teams spanning all seven functions 

 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Systems, Electrical Engineering, or related field — or equivalent verifiable experience 


 

Bonus Points for the Following: 
 
 Direct experience with constellation programs and fleet-wide conformance reporting 

 Familiarity with SAP (Special Access Program) assurance requirements 

 Prior experience as CCB chair in a high-rate production environment 

 Familiarity with CMMI or AS9100 quality management systems in a space or defense manufacturing environment 

 Range safety certification or prior direct range safety interface experience 


 

Additional Requirements: This is a fast-paced, high-impact environment - flexibility to occasionally work extended hours or weekends during critical periods is expected.

This is a full time, exempt position, based out of our Saratoga office.  The target base pay for this position is $190,000- $225,000annually.  The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  
 
We are redefining how satellites are designed, manufactured and used—so we’re looking for candidates with passion, deep knowledge and direct experience on LEO satellite component development, design and in-orbit activities. If that’s your experience – then we’ll be immediately wow-ed.
 
This role requires access to controlled technical data. Under U.S. law (ITAR/EAR), we can only consider U.S. persons (U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and individuals granted asylum or refugee status). 
 
E-Space is not currently able to provide employment sponsorship for candidates who do not hold work authorization for the location of this role.


Why E-Space is right for you:

As a member of our team, you will play a crucial role in driving our success.  Our team members have a strong sense of dedication and responsibility; this includes a strong commitment to our mission to create an entirely new suite of global capabilities to improve lives, business efficiencies and build a smarter planet. This means that there will be times when extra hours, including nights and weekends, may be needed to meet critical deadlines and mission goals.  In return, we offer a dynamic work environment with opportunities for professional growth and development and the chance to make a meaningful impact in a high-growth industry.  

We want you to make the most of your journey at E-Space. That’s why we support and invest in the physical, emotional and financial well-being of our team members and their families. Some of what you can expect when working at E-Space:

• An opportunity to really make a difference
• Sustainability at our core
• Fair and honest workplace
• Innovative thinking is encouraged
• Competitive salaries
• Continuous learning and development
• Health and wellness care options
• Financial solutions for the future 
• Optional legal services (US only)
• Paid holidays
• Paid time off

 At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites.  Integrated Planning
 Own the integrated operations plan covering requirements across all product lines, machines, field headcount, and material readiness.

 Identify constraints in the plan and build scenarios that drive resolution or acceptable alternatives.

 Partner with each Operations leader to surface optimizations, risks, and constraints, and develop paths to mitigation.

 Contribute to the long-term forecast, integrating priorities across multiple teams.

 Track lead times and drive alignment on critical decision timelines and order dates.

 Work with Operations leaders to plan labor availability, using key ratios and operational planning drivers.

 Core operational metrics defined, tracked, and reviewed on a regular rhythm.
