existing_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing Engineering
existing_roles.description:
About Formlabs: 

 Do you want to change how the world creates?

 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.

 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.

 Formlabs is manufacturing thousands of printers, an enormous task – and the complexity will grow as we build tens and even hundreds of thousands of electronic products each year. We are looking for someone who will lead the process to take newly innovated products to mass production. 

 If you are a seasoned manufacturing leader who has brought new products to market, we want you to join our team as our Head of Manufacturing Engineering. 

 The Job: 

 
 Manage a direct team of 15+ manufacturing engineers, manufacturing software engineers and program managers responsible for developing and maintaining the manufacturing tools, systems and processes that bring Formlabs products to the market 

 Lead the operationalizing of our products through strong program management processes that define and execute requirements from both design and operations teams  

 Develop strong processes and NPI accountability crossfades to bring great products to the market via leadership in DFM, DTC & DFQ areas 

 Aggressive cost management to facilitate speed to market and then market leading cost structures of components and finished products 

 Take design intent manufacturing tools/processes and operationalize those for high volume, consistent quality and low cost manufacturing 

 Integrate process discipline, hardware fixtures, software calibration routines and strong management tools to launch and optimize production processes 

 Lead and enable Formlabs and 3rd party manufacturing sites globally  

 Expand the manufacturing capabilities of our global supply chain to include new vertically integrated functions as well as additional outsourced capabilities, including ODM, JDM, white labeled) to meet the growing product requirements of Formlabs 

 Forward thinking strategy of how to ensure Formlabs manufacturing continues to be a strategic advantage and industry disrupter 

 Build people, processes and technology to enable Formlabs continued business growth 

 
   You:   

 
 A leader who can hire, manage and develop a team of diverse supply chain, manufacturing and engineering professionals 

 Highly technical manufacturing/operations leader 

 NPI experience bringing new electro-mechanical products to market  

 Experience managing leveraging partnerships in Asia to bring products to market 

 Have built organizations and processes for high growth companies 

 Experience with budget and business plan development 

 A driving change agent 

 
 Our Benefits & Perks: 

 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs

 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)

 401K matching and access to financial advisors

 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)

 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it

 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats

 Regular sponsored professional development opportunities

 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

 And of course… unlimited 3D prints

 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.   

 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

  
 Compensation: 
 

 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.

 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

 The annual base pay range for this role is:
 $175,000 — $300,000 USD

existing_roles.title: Operations Director
existing_roles.description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route.

Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

 Position Summary 

 The Operations Director is responsible for leading and coordinating key operational functions of the manufacturing facility, including Production Planning, Supply Chain, Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), and Infrastructure/Construction Engineering .

 This position plays a critical role in ensuring production readiness, material availability, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, facility development, and cross-functional execution.

 The Operations Director will work closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Finance, Human Resources, and other functional leaders to support safe, efficient, and scalable operations of the Chicago manufacturing facility.

 Key Responsibilities 

 
 Production Planning & Operations Coordination 

 
 
 Lead production planning and scheduling based on demand, capacity, materials, and priorities.

 Develop and manage short- and long-term production plans.

 Coordinate manpower, equipment, and materials to achieve production targets.

 Monitor plan execution and identify delivery risks.

 Drive cross-functional efforts to resolve production and operational constraints.

 Track key KPIs, including production attainment, inventory, material availability, delivery, and efficiency.

 Support S&OP and capacity planning processes.

 
 
 Supply Chain Management 

 
 
 Lead plant supply chain operations, including production planning, materials, procurement, inventory, warehousing, and logistics.

 Ensure material availability while maintaining optimal inventory levels.

 Improve inventory turnover and reduce excess and obsolete stock.

 Drive supplier performance and supply continuity.

 Identify supply chain risks and implement contingency plans.

 Manage domestic and international logistics activities.

 Lead continuous improvement in cost, efficiency, and delivery performance.

 
 
 Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) 

 
 
 Lead the plant’s EHS programs and team to ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.

 Promote a strong safety culture and drive workplace safety initiatives.

 Oversee inspections, risk assessments, corrective actions, and emergency preparedness.

 Monitor EHS performance and implement corrective actions as needed.

 Partner with cross-functional teams to improve safety and compliance.

 Support regulatory audits, inspections, and permitting activities.

 
 
 Infrastructure & Construction Engineering 

 
 
 Lead facility engineering, infrastructure, and construction projects supporting plant operations.

 Oversee plant expansion, renovations, and infrastructure improvements.

 Manage contractors, vendors, and project stakeholders.

 Ensure projects meet scope, budget, schedule, quality, and safety requirements.

 Maintain critical facility systems, utilities, and infrastructure readiness.

 Support production line installation, commissioning, and facility startup activities.

 
 
 Operational Excellence & Cross-Functional Management 

 
 
 Establish and manage operational processes across planning, supply chain, EHS, and infrastructure.

 Lead operational reviews and drive action item completion.

 Identify and escalate operational risks to plant leadership.

 Implement continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, cost, delivery, inventory, and efficiency.

 Drive KPI-based decision-making and operational visibility.

 Support ERP/MRP and digitalization initiatives.

 Foster collaboration across Operations, Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Finance, HR, and IT.

 
 
 Team Leadership 

 
 
 Lead, develop, and mentor managers and operational teams.

 Establish organizational structure, goals, and succession plans.

 Recruit, develop, and retain key talent.

 Drive performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.

 Foster a collaborative, safety-focused, high-performance culture.

 
 Qualifications 

 
 Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field required.

 Master's degree or MBA preferred.

 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, supply chain, production planning, engineering, or related functions.

 5+ years of leadership experience managing managers and/or multiple operational functions.

 Strong experience in large-scale manufacturing environments.

 Demonstrated experience in production planning, supply chain management, and plant operations.

 Working knowledge of EHS management and U.S. regulatory requirements.

 Experience supporting facility construction, plant expansion, infrastructure, or manufacturing engineering projects strongly preferred.

 Strong knowledge of ERP/MRP systems; SAP experience preferred.

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Experience in lithium-ion battery, EV, automotive, energy storage, electronics, or advanced manufacturing .

 Experience supporting the launch or ramp-up of a new manufacturing facility in the United States.

 Experience managing complex global supply chains.

 Familiarity with high-volume automated manufacturing environments.

 Experience working with international and cross-cultural teams.

 Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, S&OP, inventory optimization, and operational excellence methodologies.

 PMP, APICS/CPIM/CSCP, Six Sigma, or related professional certification is a plus.

 
 Key Performance Indicators 

 Key performance measures may include:

 Production Planning: Production Plan Attainment | Capacity Utilization | Schedule Adherence

 Supply Chain: On-Time Delivery | Material Availability | Inventory Turns | Inventory Accuracy | Logistics Cost

 EHS: Safety Incident Rate | Corrective Action Closure | Regulatory Compliance | Environmental Performance

 Infrastructure: Project Schedule | Project Budget | Construction Safety | Facility Readiness | Utility Reliability

 Overall Operations: Cost Reduction | Operational Efficiency | Risk Management | Cross-Functional Execution

 Leadership Scope 

 The Operations Director provides leadership and management oversight for:

 Production Planning / PMC 

 Supply Chain & Logistics 

 Warehouse & Inventory 

 Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) 

 Infrastructure / Construction / Facility Engineering   

  

 

 The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $200,000.00 –$240,000.00, plus eligibility for 20% bonus and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by factors such as the role, level, and geographic location. The range listed in the job posting represents the minimum and maximum target salaries for this position across all U.S. locations. Actual compensation within the range will be influenced by the specific work location, along with factors such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter will provide more details about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. Please note that the listed compensation reflects the base salary only and does not include bonus or benefits.

existing_roles.description:
Job Title: Director of Quality
 Employment Status: Full-time
 Office Hours: Monday - Friday; hybrid schedule
 Location: Boston, Massachusetts
 Compensation: $150,000 - $185,000, plus equity options. (Compensation dependent on experience level)

 
 The Director of Quality owns Ketryx's Quality Management System (QMS), Information Security Management System (ISMS), AI governance program, and certification portfolio. This leader keeps our processes effective, scalable, and audit-ready while helping the business ship and serve enterprise customers efficiently. Because Ketryx builds compliance software for regulated industries, the role is also an internal reference user of our platform and a public voice on quality and regulatory practice.

 What You'll Do 

 
 Own the QMS and support the ISMS: Keep policies, SOPs, and records aligned with how we operate, including ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 programs.

 Lead AI governance: Own AI policies and ISO/IEC 42001 conformity, and set assurance expectations for validated AI agents.

 Run audits and certifications: Lead readiness and execution for ISO 13485, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, IEC 61508, and ISO 26262, plus customer audits and supplier assessments.

 Govern change and release: Define risk-based gates and evidence expectations, and own release-level risk assessments.

 Enable customers and deals: Maintain validation packages and the trust center, and support questionnaires, RFPs, and strategic accounts where compliance is a blocker.

 Track regulation: Monitor emerging requirements (e.g., EU MDR, EU Cyber Resilience Act, 21 CFR Part 11) and translate them into internal and customer guidance.

 Lead the QA/RA consulting team: Staff engagements, set deliverable standards, provide final review, and develop consultants.

 Partner across the company: Work with Engineering, Product, Security, Sales, and leadership, and represent Ketryx externally through content, conferences, and standards work.

 
 How Success Is Measured 

 
 Zero major nonconformities in certification audits, with findings closed on time

 All committed certifications achieved or maintained, including ISO 26262 by August 2027

 Validation packages and risk assessments published for every platform release

 Fast, reliable responses to customer compliance inquiries and deal blockers

 High-quality consulting deliverables with zero quality-related escalations

 
 What We're Looking For 

 
 10+ years of experience in quality at a MedTech, BioPharma, or Life Sciences company

 Track record operating or leading a QMS and supporting external audits in a regulated environment

 Experience owning or materially supporting an ISMS under ISO/IEC 27001 or equivalent

 Strong command of risk-based quality practices and change and release governance

 Clear communicator with technical and non-technical audiences, with strong documentation skills

 
 Nice to Have 

 
 Hands-on audit experience across ISO 13485, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, ISO/IEC 42001, IEC 61508, ISO 26262, and SOC 2

 Experience with AI governance and validating AI-enabled features

 Background supporting customer validation and security questionnaires for enterprise SaaS

 Familiarity with functional safety tool qualification

 Experience leading a team of quality or regulatory professionals

 What We Offer

 
 Competitive compensation

 Generous stock options possible

 Work in an exciting field with a positive impact on the world

 Opportunity to learn and grow as part of a global team

 Generous PTO for full-time

 
 Ketryx is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances

 Ketryx is saving and improving lives by making medical software safe and reliable. We empower software teams building medical applications to create safe, secure, and compliant products used by patients and providers worldwide. We believe that, by automating much of the documentation and quality processes, teams will be able to produce safer and more innovative medical software faster.

 Ketryx is at the forefront of helping teams incorporate AI/ML into medical software and that’s why we need you!

existing_roles.title: Executive Director, Supply Chain & External Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
Company Overview: 

 Prime Medicine is a leading biotechnology company dedicated to creating and delivering the next generation of gene editing therapies to patients. The Company is leveraging its proprietary Prime Editing platform, a versatile, precise and efficient gene editing technology, to develop a new class of differentiated, one-time, potentially curative genetic therapies. Designed to make only the right edit at the right position within a gene while minimizing unwanted DNA modifications, Prime Editors have the potential to repair almost all types of genetic mutations and work in many different tissues, organs and cell types.  

 Prime Medicine is currently progressing a diversified portfolio of investigational therapeutic programs organized around our core areas of focus: hematology, immunology & oncology, liver and lung. Across each core area, Prime Medicine is focused initially on a set of high value programs, each targeting a disease with well-understood biology and a clearly defined clinical development and regulatory path, and each expected to provide the foundation for expansion into additional opportunities. For more information, please visit www.primemedicine.com .

 Prime Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company creating the next generation of gene editing therapies. Our Prime Editing platform is versatile, precise, and efficient, with the potential to address more than 90% of known disease-causing genetic mutations. We have three programs in the clinic: an ex vivo cell therapy for an ultra-rare disease advancing toward a Biologics License Application (BLA), and two in vivo liver-targeting LNP Prime Editor programs, with more in development. We are a mission-driven team working in a lean, fast-moving environment.

 Position Overview

 Reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer, the Executive Director of Supply Chain and External Manufacturing is a member of the Technology, Development and Operations (TDO) leadership team. You will own Prime Medicine’s end-to-end supply chain, from raw materials through clinical supply and commercialization, with direct accountability for materials management and for supporting internal planning and manufacturing needs. You will manage our external manufacturing partners, lead a highly functional lean team, and serve as the primary partner to Finance for TDO external spend. We are looking for a leader who embraces AI as a core part of how supply chain and external manufacturing run at Prime Medicine, from forecasting and materials visibility to partner performance and cost modeling. This role is for someone who thrives in ambiguity, is energized by building, and pairs strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

 Primary Responsibilities

 
 Partner with the CTO and TDO leadership to define manufacturing and supply chain strategy, including network design, make-vs-buy decisions, and partner selection.

 AI-enabled operations. Lead the use of AI and digital tools across supply chain and external manufacturing, including demand forecasting, materials and inventory visibility, partner performance monitoring, contract and cost modeling, and logistics tracking, as well as keeping the function ahead of new tools as they emerge.

 Materials management. Own materials management across the portfolio, including forecasting, sourcing, purchasing, and inventory of raw materials, critical starting materials, and components, so materials are available on time for each program.

 Planning and supply operations. Support internal planning and the manufacturing needs of each program; deliver labeling, packaging, shipping, and cell therapy logistics on time and in full; and resolve supply risks before they affect timelines.

 External manufacturing and partners. Build and manage a network of CDMOs, CROs, and critical suppliers, including contracts, governance, performance, and qualification of new partners.

 Clinical and commercial readiness. Ensure supply chain documentation and external site readiness support IND and BLA submissions, working with CMC, Regulatory, Quality, Non-clinical Development, Clinical, and program teams.

 Own TDO budget development for external spend, cost projections, and financial reporting in close partnership with functional leaders and Finance.

 Leadership . Lead, coach, and inspire your team of supply chain/external manufacturing professionals and indirect colleagues across TDO; foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaborative problem-solving and goal attainment

 
 Preferred Qualifications

 
 Bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical discipline; advanced degree (MS, MBA, or PhD) preferred

 15–20+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, technical operations, external manufacturing, process development, or MSAT within biotech or pharma

 Direct ownership of materials management and clinical supply for clinical-stage programs

 Experience managing CDMOs and CROs, including negotiating MSAs and SOWs

 Experience with cell therapy and/or LNP or nucleic acid programs; experience supporting IND/CTA and BLA/MAA submissions

 Financial acumen, including ownership of operating budgets and multi-year cost projections

 Track record of implementing AI or digital tools that improved forecasting, visibility, or decision-making in supply chain or operations, and of changing how teams work as a result

 Strong change management, project management, and communication skills, with the ability to build trust with partners, Finance, and senior leadership

 Plus: lean, fast-moving biotech; ultra-rare disease or small patient population experience

 
 Why Prime Medicine

 Your work will matter: our programs have the potential to be curative therapies for patients with no other options, and this role directly enables that. You will be part of the TDO leadership team, with direct access to the CTO and interact with other Executive leaders, and you will shape how AI is applied to supply chain and manufacturing at a company where it is a growing priority. You will have ownership from day one in building how Prime Medicine delivers for patients.

 Prime Medicine is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law.

 Location: Cambridge, MA | Reports to: Chief Technology Officer | TDO Leadership Team Member
 The pay range reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity).

 Prime Medicine offers a comprehensive Total Rewards package with robust health, financial, and wellness benefits—including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) match, and equity programs—along with generous paid time off, wellness days, and company-wide recharge breaks.

 Our commitment to employee well-being reflects our belief that when we care for our people, we strengthen our ability to put patients first and make meaningful impact together.

existing_roles.description:
About Re:Build  

 At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.  

 We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.  

 The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate.  (link to  The Re:Build Way principles )  

 Who We Are Looking For 

 Re:Build Harness Solutions is looking for an experienced manufacturing leader to lead wire harness operations at our Kalamazoo, Michigan facility. You bring direct experience in wire harness, cable assembly, or electro-mechanical manufacturing and know how to build safe, reliable operations that deliver on quality, cost, and customer commitments.

 You are a hands-on, metrics-driven leader who develops strong teams and scalable manufacturing systems. You use measures such as OEE, first-pass yield, cycle time, labor efficiency, safety, and on-time delivery to drive improvement and make informed decisions.

 This is an opportunity to help build a digitally integrated wire harness operation and establish the processes, technology, and workforce capabilities needed to support continued growth.

 What You Get To Do 

 
 Lead daily manufacturing operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and customer priorities.

 Drive production performance using KPIs including OEE, first-pass yield, on-time delivery, cycle time, and labor efficiency.

 Optimize wire harness processes including cutting, stripping, crimping, soldering, assembly, testing, and inspection.

 Implement wire processing equipment, automated systems, smartBuild formboards, tooling, and digital manufacturing technologies.

 Lead Lean continuous improvement efforts to reduce waste, improve quality, and increase production efficiency.

 Partner with Engineering on manufacturability, capacity, production requirements, and process improvements.

 Build and develop a high-performing team of supervisors, engineers, technicians, and production operators.

 Own plant safety, quality, and compliance, including applicable IPC/WHMA-A-620, AS9100, ISO 13485, and ITAR requirements.

 Lead root cause analysis, corrective actions, quality audits, inspection, and testing activities.

 Manage key plant financial drivers, capital equipment investments, manufacturing costs, and capacity planning.

 Support customer requirements, quoting, business reviews, and strategic growth initiatives.

 
 What You Bring To The Team 

 
 10+ years of manufacturing operations experience, including 5+ years in plant or production management leading teams of 20+.

 Direct wire harness, cable assembly, or electro-mechanical manufacturing experience.

 Experience scaling low-volume, high-mix operations and improving quality, cost, and delivery.

 Strong knowledge of wire cutting, stripping, crimping, soldering, assembly, testing, and wire harness workmanship standards.

 Hands-on experience with wire processing equipment such as Komax, Schleuniger, or equivalent systems.

 Knowledge of IPC/WHMA-A-620 and familiarity with ITAR-controlled manufacturing environments.

 Strong Lean manufacturing and structured problem-solving experience, including 5S, standard work, visual management, A3, or 8D.

 Experience with ERP/MES systems, production metrics, capacity planning, scheduling, and manufacturing flow.

 Demonstrated ability to build teams, coach employees, and lead through growth or operational transformation.

 Ability to work onsite in Kalamazoo, Michigan and travel up to 10%.

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 IPC/WHMA-A-620 Certified IPC Specialist or Trainer.

 AS9100 or ISO 9001 Lead Auditor certification.

 Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt.

 OSHA certification.

 
 Compensation  

 The base salary range for this position is $120,000 – $180,000 per year. This range represents the Company’s good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting.  Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits. 

 The BIG payoff 

 We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.  Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

 We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate 

 Re:Build Manufacturing is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason.

 Re:Build is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at accommodations.ta@ReBuildmanufacturing.com or you may call us at 617.909.6275.

existing_roles.title: Vice President, Head of Quality Assurance
existing_roles.description:
Vice President, Head of Quality Assurance

 About the Role

 The Vice President, Head of Quality Assurance provides strategic and operational leadership of GxP quality across manufacturing, laboratory, distribution, pharmacovigilance, and external partner activities from early clinical development through product approval. This individual will lead the continued development, implementation, and maintenance of scalable, phase-appropriate Quality systems and governance frameworks to support CMC development, clinical manufacturing, and inspection readiness, while building a foundation that can scale as the company’s programs advance toward registration and approval. The VP will partner with CMC, Clinical Operations, Regulatory, Biomarkers, Safety, and Clinical, and with external CDMO, CRO, and laboratory partners, to ensure compliance with applicable global regulations and to sustain a strong culture of quality, integrity, patient safety, and data integrity.

 Responsibilities

 
 Serve as the executive owner of quality, setting quality strategy and priorities in line with company objectives and development milestones, and representing Quality across the organization.

 Build, lead, and develop a quality assurance organization capable of supporting Treeline’s growing global manufacturing, laboratory, and clinical activities and positioned to scale as programs advance.

 Own and continue to develop Treeline’s Quality Management System in a phase-appropriate, scalable manner, ensuring adherence to applicable global GxP requirements and industry standards, including management review and quality council governance.

 Define and drive a pragmatic, data-driven Quality strategy, and establish governance frameworks, escalation pathways, and quality metrics that enable proactive risk management and informed decision-making.

 Provide quality oversight of CDMOs, contract laboratories, including supplier qualification, quality agreements, audit programs, and ongoing performance management.

 Plan, oversee, and complete audits of manufacturing, laboratory, and distribution partners, and of clinical vendors and sites through a risk-based audit program.

 Lead external Health Authority inspections, internal audits, and inspection readiness activities and build toward pre-approval inspection readiness.

 Review and approve analytical documentation, including methods, validation protocols and reports, specifications, and stability protocols and reports, and manage expiry extensions.

 Provide Quality input into CMC activities, including process development, tech transfer, manufacturing scale-up, equipment qualification, and process validation and PPQ strategy as programs mature toward registration.

 Hold accountability for final release or other disposition of clinical trial material, including country-specific release requirements and collaboration with Qualified Persons (QPs).

 Ensure effective oversight and timely resolution of deviations, investigations, OOS/OOT results, CAPAs, change controls, and product complaints, seeking input from relevant departments so that Quality impact is fully evaluated.

 Review and approve clinical product labels and the quality aspects of IMPD/IND/NDA CMC sections.

 Oversee quality aspects of the clinical supply chain and distribution (GDP), including temperature control, storage, shipping, and returns.

 Oversee pharmacovigilance quality activities to ensure compliance, data integrity, and effective safety surveillance.

 Ensure appropriate quality oversight of clinical trial execution and GCP compliance, in partnership with Clinical Operations.

 Drive consistency in quality processes, risk management approaches, computerized system validation, and data integrity standards across the organization.

 Author, review, and approve SOPs, policies, and controlled quality documentation.

 Keep current with global health authority laws, regulations, and guidance; identify gaps and implement process improvements resulting from new or revised requirements.

 Anticipate quality requirements for later-stage development, registration, and approval, and plan systems and resourcing accordingly so the Quality Management System can scale without rework.

 Manage the Quality budget and resourcing, and participate in project teams and sub-teams as needed.

 
 Required Qualifications

 
 BA/BS in Science, Engineering, or a related discipline required; advanced degree (MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) preferred.

 15+ years of Quality Assurance experience in an FDA-regulated biotech or pharmaceutical environment, with increasing levels of responsibility, including leadership of a quality function.

 5+ years of hands-on experience in one or more technical disciplines before transitioning into QA: Chemical Development/Manufacturing, Drug Product Development/Manufacturing, or Analytical Development.

 Demonstrated success building and leading a quality organization that supports a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company.

 Demonstrated success supporting programs through clinical development; experience with late-stage development, NDA/MAA submissions, and pre-approval inspections is a plus.

 Mastery of global GxP requirements and applicable international regulations and guidelines.

 Deep expertise in batch review and disposition for clinical-phase products.

 Expertise authoring and reviewing SOPs, deviations, investigations, CAPAs, and change controls, and in OOS/OOT management.

 Expertise performing and managing Quality audits and regulatory inspections.

 Demonstrated understanding of issue management, risk management, and CAPA effectiveness in manufacturing, laboratory, and clinical environments.

 Expertise overseeing quality aspects of global vendor networks, including CDMOs, contract laboratories, and distribution partners.

 Working knowledge of data integrity and computerized system validation requirements.

 Strong collaboration skills and sufficient technical acumen to partner effectively with CMC, Regulatory, Clinical Operations, Supply Chain, and other key stakeholders.

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong executive presence and the ability to influence at all levels of the organization.

 Ability to manage competing priorities and timelines in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

 Strong problem-solving skills and ability to implement scalable Quality Systems improvements.

 Demonstrated commitment to quality, compliance, patient safety, and data integrity.

 Working knowledge of oncology drug development preferred.

 
  

 This position is classified as exempt. The anticipated annual base salary range for candidates who will work in Watertown, MA is $285,000 - $350,000. The final base salary offered to the successful candidate will be dependent upon several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and length of experience within the job, type and length of experience within the job, education, and other factors. Treeline Biosciences is a multi-state employer, and this salary range may not reflect positions that work in other cities or states. 

   

  

 Recruitment fraud statement 

 Please be aware of recruitment fraud and related job scams, where scammers present themselves as recruiters but are seeking to steal money or personal information. Keep the following in mind to protect yourself: 

 
 Treeline Biosciences will never ask for money from you as part of our recruitment process. Do not provide bank details or pay somebody for the promise of a job at Treeline. 

 We do not conduct interviews through RingCentral, Skype or Telegram. 

 Our job openings are first posted to treeline.bio/careers. If you locate a listing for a Treeline job on another site, please ensure it is also posted on our careers website. 

 You can find more information about job scams at consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams. 

 To report job scams, head to ReportFraud.ftc.gov. 

 
  

  

  
 Notice to Search Firms/Third-Party Recruitment Agencies (Recruiters)

 The Human Resources team manages the recruitment and employment process for Treeline Biosciences. To protect the interests of all parties involved, Treeline Biosciences will only accept resumes from a recruiter if an executed search agreement directed to the particular position or positions is in place at the start of the recruitment effort. Unsolicited resumes sent to Treeline Biosciences from recruiters do not constitute any type of relationship between the recruiter and Treeline Biosciences and do not obligate Treeline Biosciences in any way to pay fees should we hire from those resumes. Recruiters are requested not to contact or present candidates directly to our hiring manager or employees.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

 DIRECTOR, SITE OPERATIONS 

 As the Director of Site Operations, you’ll own node and rack uptime for SpaceXSI's AI supercompute cluster—the most advanced of its kind. This role is the extreme owner of cluster health and customer Service Level Agreements across 5+ sites operating 24/7. You’ll lead a 250+ person organization of site managers, shift supervisors, and technicians, plus the site reliability engineering team that monitors cluster health and drives fault mitigation at scale. We’re looking for a hands-on operations leader who can build a culture of excellence and accountability, partner tightly across the company, and keep uptime exceptional as we grow.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Own cluster uptime by serving as extreme owner of node, rack, and cluster health across 5+ sites running 24/7, accountable for customer Service Level Agreements and consistently exceptional uptime on SpaceXSI's supercompute cluster

 Lead a large operations organization, directing a 250+ person team spanning site managers, shift supervisors, and technicians across four 24/7 shifts, building a culture of excellence and accountability at every layer of the org

 Drive node and rack remediation by ensuring systematic recovery of failed nodes and racks through command-line and physical intervention, driving mean time to repair to the feasible minimum

 Partner across functions by coordinating with facilities operations to limit downtime from power and cooling faults and proactive maintenance; with network engineering on cluster upgrades; and with tenant representatives on node remediation and planned and unplanned downtime

 Own vendor execution, directing vendors through hardware rework and field operations so repairs, replacements, and capacity work happen at the speed the cluster requires

 Lead site reliability engineering, owning the SRE organization responsible for proactive cluster health monitoring, reactive fault mitigation at scale, root cause analyses for node, rack, and cluster issues, and site-wide reliability procedures and fault documentation

 Run data-driven improvement by leading continual improvement and efficiency initiatives, using operational data to balance team resources and raise uptime, repair time, and SLA performance across sites

 Command incidents at scale and set the standard for incident response during cluster-impacting events, providing clear direction, fast recovery, and tight communication with internal and external partners

 Scale operations by standardizing best practices across sites and grow the organization in step with cluster expansion, keeping operations consistent as SpaceXSI's footprint scales

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree and 7+ years of experience working in a large scale operations with 5+ years leading people leaders of technical teams; OR 10+ years of experience working in a large scale operations with 5+ years leading people leaders of technical teams

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Proven ability to lead large, multi-site, 24/7 operations organizations in fast-paced, high-responsibility settings

 Deep expertise in server hardware, cluster reliability, and data center technologies, from deployment through lifecycle management

 Experience supporting compute-heavy environments like AI, machine learning, or high-performance computing at scale

 A track record of owning uptime, Service Level Agreements, or reliability metrics for large compute clusters

 Experience leading site reliability engineering or equivalent reliability-focused teams, including root cause analysis and procedure ownership

 Strong analytical skills and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences, from technicians to executive and tenant partners

 A history of partnering with vendors at scale, driving mean time to repair down, and scaling operations across multiple sites

 Familiarity with tooling and automation (e.g., Jira, Python, Bash) used to monitor cluster health and improve team efficiency

 Enthusiasm for SpaceXSI's mission to accelerate human discovery and unravel the universe

 Ability to thrive in a dynamic, mission-focused environment with on-call ownership of cluster-impacting events

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 Willingness to travel frequently to data center locations to support operations across sites

 Physical capability to handle data center tasks, including lifting up to 50 lbs unassisted, standing for long periods, and occasional ladder use

 Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed

 The Sr. Manager of Memphis Power Plant Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the gas turbine power generation facility supporting SpaceXSI's Colossus data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee. This role oversees all plant operations, maintenance, commissioning, and continued construction/expansion of the dedicated power plant, with full ownership of delivering reliable, high-availability electrical power to the Colossus AI training clusters. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence, ensuring 24/7 power reliability and quality, safety, environmental compliance, and leading cross-functional teams to achieve aggressive scale-up, availability, cost, and schedule objectives in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Memphis gas turbine power plant, including 24/7 operations, maintenance, commissioning, and ongoing construction and capacity expansion

 Own end-to-end delivery of electrical power to the Colossus data center sites, ensuring industry-leading reliability, availability, power quality, and redundancy

 Lead multidisciplinary teams of operators, maintenance technicians, engineers, contractors, and support staff in a 24/7 operational and construction environment

 Oversee plant performance, commissioning, testing, and seamless integration with data center electrical infrastructure and load

 Develop and execute comprehensive operations and maintenance strategies, including preventative/predictive maintenance, outage planning, hot gas path management, and OEM coordination for gas turbines, generators, balance of plant, and high-voltage electrical systems

 Manage concurrent construction, equipment installation, civil works, and phased capacity expansions while maintaining safe, reliable operation of the existing plant

 Ensure full compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements, including air permits, emissions controls, TDEC, EPA, OSHA, and local authorities

 Partner closely with SpaceXSI data center operations, engineering, fuel suppliers, OEMs, utilities, and regulatory agencies

 Formulate and execute operating budgets, fuel management, O&M, capital projects, and annual operating plans

 Drive continuous improvement in plant availability, heat rate, emissions, cost, safety metrics, and operational processes

 Establish and promote a culture of uncompromising safety, accountability, operational excellence, rapid execution, and collaboration

 Serve as the site leader and primary representative to the Memphis community, regulators, and stakeholders

 Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing talent; manage staffing, resource allocation, and contractor oversight for both operations and construction

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree 

 8+ years of experience in power generation operations, plant management, or industrial or aerospace operations

 3+ years of leadership experience managing teams of operators, technicians, and engineers

 Experience operating or managing gas turbine power plants (simple cycle or combined cycle)

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Experience managing large-scale gas turbine facilities (100 MW+), preferably with high-availability critical power applications (data centers, industrial, or similar)

 Proven track record of achieving and sustaining high plant availability, reliability, and low forced outage rates

 Hands-on experience with plant construction, commissioning, start-up, and concurrent operations/expansion of gas turbine facilities

 Deep knowledge of gas turbine technology (aeroderivative and/or heavy-duty frames), performance optimization, emissions controls (SCR, etc.), and balance of plant systems

 Experience with high-voltage electrical systems, generators, switchgear, protection, and data center or industrial interconnection

 Strong understanding of environmental permitting, air quality compliance, and regulatory reporting for combustion turbines

 Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments requiring simultaneous operations and major construction

 Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, fuel costs, contractors, and complex stakeholder relationships

 Excellent oral and written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills

 Unfazed by major, abrupt changes in strategic direction or aggressive timelines

 Ability to work in a demanding, autonomously driven, start-up atmosphere

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 Ability to support and supervise plant operations and construction outside of normal business hours, including nights, weekends, and on-call response

 Must be based at the Memphis/Southaven site

 Willingness to work extended hours as needed to support plant reliability and construction milestones

 General physical fitness required; ability to walk the plant site, access equipment, and work in industrial/outdoor environments (heat, noise, etc.)

Responsibilities: 

 Define and implement Crescent's phase-appropriate QC strategy and operating model across early development, Phase 3, PPQ, regulatory submission, and commercialization, with clear decision rights and handoffs among Analytical Sciences, QC, and GMP QA.

 Oversee QC activities for drug substance, drug product, intermediates, finished goods, in-process, release, characterization, and stability testing across the portfolio.

 Partner with Analytical Sciences on integrated Phase 3 and PPQ readiness, including method validation and transfer, laboratory qualification, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, stability, sample management, and testing timelines.

 Partner with Analytical Sciences, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, and QA on specifications and stability strategy; lead operational implementation, stability execution, data review, trending, and escalation within the QC network.

 Provide technical leadership for OOS, OOT, OOE, atypical results, invalid assays, laboratory deviations, CAPAs, and change controls, ensuring scientifically sound, timely investigations and risk-based escalation.

 Lead selection, onboarding, qualification, governance, and performance management of CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including agreements, capacity, metrics, issue management, data integrity, and inspection readiness.

 Provide QC input to CMC and regulatory strategies and support IND/IMPD, BLA/MAA, health authority, and inspection activities; ensure commitments are implemented within the laboratory network.

 Lead alliance management with business partners on QC matters, including governance, roles and responsibilities, shared testing and release requirements, issue escalation, decision-making, and alignment on development, regulatory, and future commercial priorities.

 Establish scalable QC procedures, systems, metrics, budgeting, forecasting, and resource plans; support compliant use of LIMS, stability, analytical data, and trending tools, and build internal QC capability as Crescent advances toward commercialization.

 Mentor staff and consultants and foster a culture of scientific rigor, collaboration, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement while staying current with evolving GMP, ICH, compendial, and industry expectations.

 Bachelor's degree in life sciences, analytical sciences, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.

 Experience supporting biologics from clinical development through Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA, and commercial readiness; bispecific antibody, ADC, or other complex modality experience is a plus.

 Proven experience transitioning methods from development into routine GMP QC use, including qualification, validation, transfer, implementation, performance monitoring, and lifecycle management.

 Ability to establish clear roles and effective collaboration among Analytical Sciences, QC, GMP QA, CMC/Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and external partners.

 Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach, solutions-oriented leader who communicates clearly, applies pragmatic science- and risk-based judgment, works effectively in a fast-paced small-company environment, and can travel to external sites as needed.

 Malta, NY
 About GlobalFoundries: 
 GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets.  Summary of Role: 
 Assess digital maturity across Fabs and refresh digital manufacturing visions, roadmaps and enablers.
 Essential Responsibilities: 
 Assess digital maturity across Fabs and refresh digital manufacturing visions, roadmaps and enablers. Collaborate with Fab operations team across all levels to review operations pain points and performance gaps, scope digital use cases, build business cases, work with Digital Ecosystem Partnership team and GFIT to outline “make”, “buy” or “partnership” options, identify process change required and implementation risks, and set up use case teams Lead cross-functional collaboration with Legal, Finance and GFIT to establish use case valuation principles, use case go/no-go decision workflow, and data and IP risk management framework Select and coach digital translators and analysts to drive formulation of digital roadmap Support Digital Manufacturing Global Lead for executive leadership alignment and digital strategy reviews Work with Digital Manufacturing Program Office to craft change stories, develop change communication cadence across top leadership to frontline staff, identify change champions and focus areas for cultural change. Collaborate with Central Manufacturing Excellence team to embed digital use cases to Operations value creation plans. Provide leadership, coaching and mentoring to the team fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, innovation and embracing growth mindset for continuous improvement. Supervises 7 employees in Specialist Digital Mfg Strategy, Sr Specialist Digital Mfg Strategy, Sr Lead Digital Mfg Data Science, Sr Lead Digital Mfg Data Steward & Gov and Lead Digital Mfg Data Steward & Gov positions. Domestic travel once a quarter to visit a sister fab in Vermont is required.
 Other Responsibilities: 
 Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements, and programs.
 Required Qualifications: 
 Education - Master’s degree or foreign equivalent in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field of study.
 Experience – 2 years of post-baccalaureate experience in job offered or in management consulting related roles.
 Requires 2 years of experience in:
 1) Customer-centric change management
 2) complex transformation in cross-cultural international enterprises
 ) creating change management programs and their implementation including setting up tools and tracking plans
 4) presenting proposals and analyses on business decisions to top level management
 5) creating story boards and presentations, developing a plan of action to refine recommendations

existing_roles.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.  

 The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities:  we come together ,  we always look for a better way , and  we create possibilities . 

 Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

 Interested in joining us on our journey? 

he Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for plant quality performance, compliance, and continuous improvement within a high-volume manufacturing environment. This role leads the Quality Floor team and oversees production quality, component testing, Manufacturing Control Plan (MCP) auditing, and quality improvement initiatives to ensure products and processes consistently meet established standards.

Partnering closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supplier Quality, and other cross-functional teams, this leader drives structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions to reduce defects, minimize scrap and rework, and improve process capability. The Senior Manager establishes a proactive quality culture by strengthening process controls, reinforcing standard work, and using data-driven insights to identify risks and prevent recurring issues. Through strong team leadership and a focus on sustainable results, this role helps improve product reliability, reduce the cost of poor quality, and strengthen manufacturing performance. 
 Position 
Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality (Floor Leader) 
 Location 
USA, Decatur, AL 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Live, promote and support the Appliance Production System (APS) philosophy and drive continuous improvement in the quality and adjacent areas.  Coach all team members to ensure cross-functional, focused collaboration is the way we work. 
 Partner with the Product Line Quality, Business Operations and Manufacturing Engineering Leaders to promote a culture that establishes, sustains and improves product quality through engineering problem solving and discipline around supporting systems.  Promote a method-based quick response to new issues. 
 Responsible for developing team performance metrics tied to the overall factory (FPY, EOLA, Scrap) and product line financial plan (Warranty, Damage, Concessions, Scrap, Consumer Education).  Leads team to identify and complete projects and tasks supporting this effort.  Owns and assigns tasks and establishes accountability at the appropriate level.    
 Closely collaborates with the product line Engineering, Field Quality and Service organizations to understand and respond to part or system product level performance issues impacting owner use and satisfaction. Responds to this data in addition to internal data streams (leading indicators) for product quality and reliability (Engineering, EOLA and CAT / CUT labs).   
 Identify and execute projects to improve the costing of operations, broad owner for Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA), Corrective Action Request (CAR) approach to problem solving. 
 Work with Design, Operations and Quality Leadership to prioritize funding/resources to meet targets, support Continuous Improvement. 
 Owner of all attributes of the Manufacturing Control Plan for broad areas.  Responsible for the training, execution, auditing and improvement of the Manufacturing Quality Control Plan.  Support efforts intended to improve work station documentation process; create, update and maintain Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI’s), visual aid and alerts (single point lessons) as needed. 
 Provide technical oversight to drive the development, sustainment and continuous improvement of factory quality. 
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering or related discipline
 7+ years of experience with manufacturing quality/NPI quality projects and process improvement
 Experience with product and process Quality Management System development and implementation
 Previous team and project leadership, including demonstration of goal setting, monitoring of performance v goals and a strong feedback / development / accountability cycle 
 Must be skilled in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Minitab and Outlook.
 
 Working Conditions: 
 Working conditions are normal for a high-volume manufacturing environment.
 Working in this environment requires the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to; eye safety glasses, hearing protectors, work boots, and hard hats.
 These roles require frequent walking in a manufacturing plant environment.
 Hours & Weekends: Working off-shift and weekends may be required.
 
 
 Our Culture 
 Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 

 This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 

 By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy. 
 
 
 
 GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization. 
 
 
 GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. 
 
 GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S 
 
 
 If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail to ask.recruiting@geappliances.com

existing_roles.title: Director Production Control
existing_roles.description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact? 
   
 At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.
   
 Your greatest work is ahead! 

 Leidos Defense Manufacturing Sector is seeking a Director Production Control to join our manufacturing support team located in Huntsville, Alabama.  

 This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Production Control leader to manage site PC Managers and drive tactical, standardization of material requisitioning and production planning across our growing, nine manufacturing sites.

 If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, keep reading! 
   
 Leidos Defense Manufacturing Sector provides a diverse portfolio of systems, solutions, and services covering land, sea, air, space, and cyberspace for customers worldwide. Solutions for Defense include enterprise and mission IT, large-scale intelligence systems, command and control, geospatial and data analytics, cybersecurity, logistics, training, and intelligence analysis and operations support. Our team is solving the world’s toughest security challenges for customers with “can’t fail” missions. To explore and learn more, click here !
   
 Are you ready to make an impact? Apply and share your resume with us today! 

   
 Primary Responsibilities 
   
 This position will lead the teams that oversee all manufacturing production control activities, which include:

 Preparing / executing MRP, level-loading capacity across production work centers, firming purchase requisitions and manufacturing orders, establishing correct order policies based on Make-Buy and commodity types, and maintaining accurate lead times in the ERP part master table.  
 This requires coordination with configuration management, manufacturing engineering mBOM releases, and production scheduling.
  
 This is a key position in the growing defense sector that includes several types of manufacturing processes:
  
 Machining, welding, PCBA, cable assembly, clean rooms, painting, final assembly integration and testing.  
 As a leader across several production sites, it’s critical to develop standard processes, consistent KPI’s, daily / weekly / monthly battle rhythms, and network connections to share best practices at all levels of the enterprise.
   
 Basic Qualifications 
   
 Must have a Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business administration, or a related field from an accredited university and have at least 12 years of production control experience. 
 Must have experience with the Costpoint ERP system, as well as PLM, MES and capacity planning software programs. 
 Candidate must be proficient with Microsoft Office Products, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Project, Visio and Teams. 
 Experience leading others and working in a collaborative work environment across multiple sites and with multiple organizational levels. 
 Excellent communication and leadership skills. 
 Strong analytic and problem-solving abilities. 
 Proven track record developing and driving adherence to standardized, tactical execution processes. 
 Experience working in multiple phases of the product life cycle to include prototyping, design and development, and full release to production. 
 Candidate must be a resident of the North Alabama area or willing to relocate to the Huntsville - North Alabama, AL area. 
 Must be a US Citizen and possess (and be able to maintain) a Final Secret Clearance OR meet the eligibility to obtain (and maintain) a Secret Clearance. 
   
 Preferred Qualifications 
   
 MBA or MS degree. 
 Solumina MES experience to go along with required Costpoint ERP experience. 
 Dynafact Manufacturing System (DMS) capacity planning experience. 
 Lean manufacturing experience with Six Sigma certification. 
 Proven track record of process mapping and policy creation to drive standards that increase throughput, engages the workforce in adopting change, reduces waste, and improves quality. 
 CPIM, CSCP or CPM Certification preferred. 
 Experience with SCADA software and/or MS Power BI dashboards with the ability to write queries using data from external database sources. 
   
  HuntsvilleManufacturing 
 If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.
 
 
 Original Posting: 
October 26, 2026 
 For U.S. Positions: While subject to change based on business needs, Leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above.







 
 
 Pay Range: 
Pay Range $139,100.00 - $251,450.00 
 The Leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

 We are seeking a visionary leader to drive the transformation of our global manufacturing operations through automation and digitalization. As Director of Manufacturing Automation, you will lead the strategy, design, and implementation of advanced automation technologies across our manufacturing, assembly, packaging, and distribution processes. This role is ideal for a dynamic leader with deep technical expertise and a passion for innovation.
 
 WHAT YOU WILL EXPERIENCE IN THIS POSITION: 
 Strategic Planning & Road Mapping:   Develop and implement a comprehensive automation strategy aligned with enterprise goals. Collaborate to assess current capabilities and define future-state automation roadmaps.
 Technology Leadership & Integration:   Identify and implement modern automation solutions including robotics, AI, IoT, and human-machine interfaces. Lead feasibility studies, business case development, and project execution tracking.
 Innovation & Evaluation:   Stay ahead of emerging technologies and assess their potential impact. Propose implementation approaches considering cost-efficiency, scalability, and alignment with strategic goals.
 Automation Systems Management : Lead the design, programming, and implementation of automation systems incorporating PLCs, HMIs, robotics, and visual solutions. Secure seamless blending of automation with ERP, MES, and quality systems.
 Project Execution:   Lead multi-functional teams in the execution of automation projects from concept through commissioning. Lead capital budgets, timelines, and vendor relationships for automation initiatives.
 Process Optimization:   Find opportunities for automation in existing processes to reduce cycle time, improve quality, and lower costs. Implement continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, and other methodologies.
 Team Leadership:   Develop and lead a team of automation engineers, controls specialists, and technicians. Provide mentorship, training, and development to build internal automation capabilities.
 Data & Insights:   Drive data-driven decision-making through advanced analytics and real-time monitoring. Uncover and implement process improvements to elevate efficiency and minimize inefficiencies.
 Risk & Maturity Management:   Anticipate and mitigate risks associated with automation deployment. Support assessments of operational technology risks and automation maturity levels.
 Performance Measurement:   Define and track KPIs to measure the impact of automation initiatives on efficiency, quality, and cost. Continuously refine strategies based on performance insights.
 
 YOU HAVE: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or related field (Master’s preferred in Mechanical Engineering or Industrial Design).
 10+ years of leadership experience in manufacturing automation and transformation.
 Proven success leading global teams and large-scale automation initiatives.
 Expertise in robotics, mechatronics, AI, IoT, and vision systems.
 Deep knowledge of Industry 4.0 technologies, automation systems, data analytics, and lean manufacturing.
 Strong analytical, project management, and interpersonal skills.
 Lean Six Sigma knowledge preferred.
 Ability to travel approximately 25%, domestically and internationally.
 
 Our Global Hybrid Schedule and Core Hours: 
 At nVent, we value in-person collaboration and flexibility as key drivers of innovation and our strong, inclusive culture. We operate as an office-first, hybrid organization, where you will work in the office a minimum of four days a week, have one day of remote work, and follow core office hours daily (as determined by the local office) to ensure that you have the opportunity to connect face-to-face with teammates, problem-solve collaboratively, and elevate your employee engagement. Outside of the core hours, you will be able to adjust your start and end times in alignment with team guidelines and responsibilities. We have found success in having a structure that balances the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility many of us value. Our global, hybrid approach ensures that you will be empowered and afforded flexibility for how you manage work and life. 
 
 Pay Transparency: 
 nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.
 
 Compensation Range: $ 172,900 - $256,880 
 
 Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual or long-term incentives.
 
 WE HAVE: 
 A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day
 nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.

 Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com .

 
 
 Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work
 We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide

 Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

 
 
 Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:
 Innovative & adaptable

 Dedicated to absolute integrity

 Focused on the customer first

 Respectful and team oriented

 Optimistic and energizing

 Accountable for performance

 
 
 Benefits to support the lives of our employees

 
 Benefit Overview 
 
 At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being.  We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:
 Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.

 A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.

 At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.
