protected_roles.title: Senior Manager, QMS - Manufacturing
protected_roles.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.
 
 We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.
 
 We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.
 
 If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.
 
 About This Role: 
 Our Senior QMS Manager, Manufacturing is responsible for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continuously improving Crusoe's Quality Management System (QMS) across all manufacturing and operational facilities. Owning the enterprise QMS framework, this role ensures quality processes, controls, records, procedures, and compliance activities are effectively executed and scaled across the organization.
 Reporting into our Director of Quality, the QMS Manager partners closely with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and EHS to transition the organization from site-specific, paper-focused processes to a data-driven, risk-based, and preventive Quality Operating System. From leading internal and external audits to governing CAPA/NCR workflows, document control, and new site QMS launches, this role is pivotal in building an agile quality system that enables rapid business growth.
  
 What You'll Be Working On: 
 QMS Framework & Governance: Own and maintain the overall Quality Management System. Establish QMS policies, standards, and governance mechanisms that bridge operational gaps and scale with manufacturing expansion.

 Standards & Regulatory Compliance: Maintain organizational compliance with ISO 9001, customer standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. Monitor evolving standards and translate compliance requirements into practical operational controls.

 Audit Program Leadership: Direct the enterprise audit program—including internal, customer, supplier, certification, and regulatory audits. Oversee audit planning, execution, finding closure, and transition the company toward a proactive quality culture.

 CAPA & NCR Governance: Own enterprise nonconformance (NCR) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes. Standardize root-cause analysis (RCA), containment, and effectiveness verification while tracking systemic trends to prevent issue recurrence.

 Document & Change Control: Manage the Quality Document Management System and change-control governance. Ensure current procedures, specs, and records are accessible at points of use and prevent the use of obsolete documentation.

 Quality Records & Systems Integration: Establish quality record data governance. Partner with IT/Business Systems to integrate QMS data across ERP, MES, and inspection tools to drive enterprise-wide quality visibility.

 Quality Metrics & Management Reviews: Establish cross-site quality dashboards tracking NCR/CAPA aging, audit findings, COPQ, and training compliance. Lead periodic Quality Management Reviews with executive leadership to convert quality data into strategic decisions.

 Training & Quality Culture: Define role-based QMS training requirements, maintain competency records, and deploy quality awareness initiatives that foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

 Continuous Improvement & Process Maturity: Eliminate non-value-added quality steps, lead Lean Six Sigma projects, and establish closed-loop feedback between operational performance and QMS enhancements.

 Enterprise Quality Risk Management: Institute risk-based QMS governance. Maintain quality risk registers and ensure high-risk processes receive appropriate controls, audits, and management oversight.

 New Site Expansion: Lead QMS readiness activities for greenfield manufacturing sites, ensuring required procedures, forms, training, and controls are operational prior to production launch.

 Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the primary QMS subject-matter expert, partnering with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, and Supply Chain to drive systemic issue resolution.

  
 What You'll Bring to the Team: 
 Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or a related field.

 Professional Experience: 7+ years of experience in Quality, QMS, Quality Engineering, or Manufacturing Quality, with demonstrated success developing and scaling QMS frameworks.

 Quality Standards Expertise: Deep working knowledge of ISO 9001 standards, quality management principles, and regulatory compliance.

 Audit Management: Proven track record of planning, executing, and managing internal, customer, regulatory, and third-party certification audits.

 Root Cause & CAPA Mastery: Strong expertise in CAPA, NCR, 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

 Document & Change Control Governance: Demonstrated experience managing quality document control systems, record retention, and engineering/operational change management processes.

 Cross-Functional Leadership: Strong ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive accountability without relying solely on direct authority.

 Analytical & Communication Skills: Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills with the ability to translate complex quality data into actionable business strategies.

  
 Bonus Points: 
 Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

 Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

 ISO Implementation: Direct experience leading ISO 9001 implementation, recertification, or multi-site expansion.

 Systems & Digital Transformation: Experience implementing enterprise QMS software platforms (e.g., MasterControl, ETQ, Veeva) and integrating QMS with ERP/MES systems.

 Scaling Environment: Experience establishing QMS frameworks within fast-growing manufacturing organizations or greenfield facility launches.

 Advanced Quality Technologies: Experience leveraging AI, predictive analytics, or digital transformation tools in quality management.

protected_roles.description:
About Fluidstack
 We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 

 We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.
 
 We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply! 
 
 How We Operate
 Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

 
 The Manufacturing Team 
 Examples of key problems the team is working on 
 Scale manufacturing. Grow manufacturing capacity and capability across the full production process, with the range to take on more products and higher volume at an industry leading pace.

 Manufacture infrastructure. Build and operate a manufacturing ecosystem that delivers gigawatts of infrastructure per year.

 Be an engine for growth. Solve problems faster, think bigger, and develop yourself and your team as quickly and dynamically as the company around you.

 Role Scope 
 Own all production output at the Phoenix-area facility: throughput rate, takt adherence, quality escape rate, line uptime, and on-time shipment against customer delivery commitments.

 Drive continuous improvement across all production lines, including root-cause analysis and corrective action on every throughput or quality deviation, from the line floor up.

 Hold final product acceptance authority: nothing ships without your sign-off or explicit delegation, and you own the workforce interface with the on-site staffing partner to enforce that standard.

 Own site readiness across tooling, fixturing, material flow, equipment, utilities, and floor layout, including all contractor and vendor relationships and full OSHA, NFPA 70E, and air quality permit compliance.

 Build and develop the on-site manufacturing team, including production managers, supervisors, quality, and facilities staff, and own workforce planning across headcount ramp, shift structure, skill mix, and certification tracking.

 What We’re Looking For 
 The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don’t fit this role exactly, tell us where you would . 
 You have run a high-volume discrete manufacturing facility end to end and can point to a specific output record: units per shift, defect rate, on-time delivery, or throughput improvement you personally drove.

 You have managed a large on-site workforce through a third-party staffing provider and held that partner accountable to production and quality targets, not just headcount.

 You have taken a facility from construction handover through first production to steady-state output and can walk through how you handled the ramp, what broke, and how you fixed it.

 You design production systems rather than inherit them: you have personally set takt times, balanced lines, written standard work, and built visual management boards for a real facility.

 OSHA 1910, NFPA 70E, and environmental permit compliance are active parts of your daily management system, not a separate function you hand off.

 You build the culture on your floor through standard work and clear escalation paths, not through personality, and your supervisors know exactly what is expected and what triggers an escalation to you.

 Bonus: Structural steel fabrication, heavy equipment assembly, or modular construction manufacturing. Lean or Six Sigma Black Belt. Experience commissioning robotic weld cells, CNC processing lines, or AGV material handling systems.

 Salary & Benefits 
 Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity)

 Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms

 Health, dental, and vision insurance

 Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms

 Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.
 Physical Requirements 
 Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

 Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

 Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

 Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

 Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.

 
 We are committed to pay equity and transparency.
 Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.
 
 Applicant Privacy Notice 
 AI Screening Notice 
 Ashby Bias Audit 
 
 You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

protected_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing Engineering
protected_roles.description:
About Us 
 Foundry Robotics is building an AI-native robotics manufacturing company focused on deploying advanced assembly and production capability for leading robotics companies and national-security-critical hardware. Basically, we’re building robots that build robots.

We are reimagining manufacturing through advanced robotics. Our mission is to rebuild the American manufacturing industry as an AI-first, assembly-focused, dual-use contract manufacturer. We aim to empower manufacturers with intelligent, efficient, and adaptable robotic systems that redefine productivity and quality. As an early member of our team, you will have a direct and significant impact on our product, culture, and ultimate success. This role is 100% in-person at our office in Emeryville, CA.
 
 The Role 
 This role is for a Head of Manufacturing Engineering who will set the technical manufacturing automation roadmap for Foundry and build the teams that execute it. Reporting to the Chief Manufacturing Officer, you will stand up and lead two groups: Manufacturing Engineering, which owns DFM/DFA for our customers, line and cell design, tooling, automation and new product launches; and Process Engineering, which owns process optimization, standard work, yield and cycle time across every program on the floor.

You are also the owner of Foundry's hardest problem. Our customers bring us different products at different volumes, and the factory has to absorb them without being rebuilt each time. That means a flexible assembly line that runs multiple products on shared stations, automation driven by foundation models rather than hand-programmed cells, autonomous material movement from dock to station, and a factory layout designed around all of it. You will decide what we build, in what order, and why, and you will be on the floor when it gets built.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Own the multi-year manufacturing automation roadmap: which operations get automated, in what sequence, with what technology, and defend it with takt, capex and risk numbers

 Design and launch a flexible assembly line that runs multiple customer products on shared stations, fixtures and conveyance, with changeovers measured in hours rather than weeks

 Partner with our software and robotics teams to deploy foundation-model-driven automation on the floor (assembly, inspection, kitting, material handling), and decide where learned automation beats fixed automation and where it does not yet

 Specify and deploy autonomous material movement (AMR/AGV fleets, kitting, line-side replenishment) so material reaches the station without a person pushing a cart

 Own the factory layout of our Emeryville facility as a living design: flow, cell boundaries, material routes, utilities and ITAR-segregated areas, working with Facilities on the physical build-out

 Build the DFM/DFA practice that turns a customer's prototype into something we can build at rate and yield, with your engineers in customer discovery and quoting to catch cost and quality problems before the PO

 Build the Process Engineering team that owns standard work, cycle time, line balance, yield, PFMEA, control plans, tooling and fixtures, and continuous improvement

 Own new product introduction from customer handoff to stable production: pilot builds, PFMEA, control plans, work instructions, capability studies and ramp

 Hire, develop and lead manufacturing and process engineers, and set the bar for engineering culture on the floor
 

 What We're Looking For 
 Founder mentality: We love people who build like it's their own company. You move fast, take ownership, and find a way through when the path isn't obvious. You have the drive to make big things happen and the judgment to take smart risks along the way. If you prefer a clearly defined lane, a predictable pace, and all the answers before you start, there's nothing wrong with that—but Foundry might not be the right fit.
 12+ years in manufacturing engineering for complex electromechanical hardware (automotive, aerospace, robotics, or consumer electronics at scale), including 5+ years leading engineers

 Launched at least one high-volume or high-mix assembly line end to end: layout, stations, tooling, conveyance, line balance and ramp

 Built an automation program, not just bought one: you can argue cell by cell where a robot, a fixture or a person is the right answer, and you have been wrong before and fixed it

 Hands-on DFM/DFA: you have sat with a customer or a design team and changed the part so it could be built

 Deep process fundamentals: PFMEA, control plans, capability studies, standard work, takt and OEE, and you can run a Kaizen and a capex review in the same week

 Hired and grown an engineering team from a handful to dozens, and can name the first three hires you would make here and why

 Equally effective at a desk and on the shop floor, in a company that is still building its factory

 Bias toward action, scrappy problem solving, and moving fast without sacrificing rigor

 Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) due to ITAR and export control requirements for the hardware we build

 
 Nice to Have (Not Required) 
 Experience applying ML-based robotics (learned grasping, vision-guided assembly, foundation-model policies) in a production setting, or close partnership with a team that has

 AMR/AGV or autonomous intralogistics deployment

 Multi-product or contract-manufacturing environment where changeover and flexibility were the constraint

 AS9100 or ITAR-controlled production exposure

 Electromechanical assembly of robots, drones, or defense hardware

 
 Why Join Us? 
 This is one of the only places where world-class manufacturing operators, mechanical engineers, robotics researchers, and software engineers sit in the same room — building production systems together.

We are committed to being deeply embedded in the U.S. industrial base. Our focus is simple: build adaptive robotic assembly systems that make American manufacturing scalable, resilient, and competitive again.

The base salary range for this full-time position in the location of Emeryville is: $200,000—$350,000 USD

 Compensation packages at Foundry Robotics for eligible roles include base salary, equity, and benefits. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position, determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, interview performance, and relevant education or training. Foundry Robotics employees in eligible roles are also granted equity based compensation, subject to Board of Director approval. You'll also receive benefits including, but not limited to: Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage, and generous PTO.

Foundry Robotics is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

The team exists so that production never stops for material. As Anduril adds production lines and new buildings, warehouse capacity limits how fast each new product can ramp. You will lead a team of managers and supervisors and several hundred hourly associates, and you will open a new campus in Long Beach. Government property and export controlled material stay in custody the whole way. This will require experience running high volume, multi site warehouse operations by the numbers: labor planned against demand, productivity measured by process, and every miss traced to a root cause.  Run the operation from data. Build the daily view of labor, productivity by process, backlog and service level by site, pulled from the system rather than from spreadsheets, and use it to staff every shift.

 Lead from the floor through daily Gemba walks, tier meetings at every site, and a steady pace of kaizen events that each target a measured problem.

 Keep government furnished property and export controlled material segregated, serialized and traceable in every flow you run.

 Hire, train and develop hourly associates and the supervisors who lead them. Manage labor to the productivity standards and staffing guidelines set for each process, and manage overtime and attrition against plan.

 Experience running warehouse operations on a warehouse management system

 Lean or Six Sigma certification, or a documented record of kaizen results

 Supervisors you hired and developed were later promoted

 Master's degree in supply chain, engineering or business

 ABOUT THE ROLE 

 We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale. 

 In this role, you will be responsible for managing a team of highly talented managers, line supervisors, and technicians who manufacture both our current key autonomous products, Fury, Barracuda, and Roadrunner, and our emerging capabilities. This is a highly dynamic role that requires both technical and frontline people management skills. This role is at the forefront of delivering exceptional customer experiences, fostering team development, and overseeing operations at Arsenal-01 and HQ. 

 As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that both manufacturing sites and operations align with the division's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, in addition to balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's manufacturing operational success. 

 Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. The ideal candidate should be energetic, highly organized, and deeply committed to scaling innovative products. While individual contributions are valued, teamwork is crucial for achieving the highest level of success while maintaining our Anduril culture above all.

protected_roles.title: Director, Production Analytics
protected_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 About the role

 The Director, Production Analytics owns Production Analytics globally: every site, every product line, and every production function across Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, Planning, and Warehousing / Material Management. The ambition is not better dashboards. It is that a division leader can tell whether they will hit rate before they miss it, and that when we argue about where to invest, the argument is settled by data rather than by whoever presents best.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 This is a player-coach role. You will lead the hardest analytical problems yourself, on the programs that matter most to the company, and build a team that can run several more in parallel. You will be judged on what you accomplish, not on how you operate: whether a program hit rate that would otherwise have slipped, whether a constraint got cleared because we saw it coming, whether a number leadership used to make a real decision came from this team.
We weigh approach over domain familiarity. The strongest analytics leaders we have are exceptional at how they attack a problem, even where they arrived without the functional background. Manufacturing depth is useful and listed below as preferred, but it does not substitute for analytical method, judgment about what matters, and the ability to drive a result through an organization.

 What you'll do

 
 Apply analytics to production’s biggest problems. Hold an evidence-backed view of what is worth the company's attention and in what order, rather than working a request list. Take the hardest two or three problems in Anduril's flagship programs and build analytics into them end to end, hands-on.

 Make the various business units in Anduril decide earlier. Shift production reporting from retrospective to leading: risk surfaced two months before the gate, not status recited on the day of it. Adoption is the deliverable. A correct dashboard nobody opens has failed.

 Turn what worked into the enterprise standard. Generalize proven capabilities into supported products, standardize the definitions the work proved out, and consolidate the duplicated reporting they replace. A standard that survives contact with a program running at rate is defensible. One written in a document is not.

 Answer what it takes to scale. Own the analytical side of a ramp from low rate to high rate, and keep a current, evidenced view of the constraints that actually bind as the company grows.

 Build the team and the foundation. Lead the consolidated analytics organization and the managers within it. Build on and in the production process/team rather than beside them. Hold the line that the various business units own master data quality while the analytics team builds the tooling that makes defects visible and cheap to fix.

 Your work should produce numbers the business can trust. Where a metric is known to be wrong, it is a defect with an owner and a date, not a caveat on a slide. Fix the data before building on top of it.

 
 Required qualifications

 
 10+ years in analytics, data, or quantitative operations, including 5+ years leading analytics or data teams, and experience managing managers or clear readiness to do so.

 A rigorous, teachable approach to ambiguous problems. You can describe how you decide what to work on, how you structure an analysis, how you know when you're wrong, and how you install that method in a team.

 Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL and a modern data stack, able to get into a dataset personally, find the answer, and defend the method. This role does not succeed as pure management.

 Demonstrated ability to identify the highest-value problem in a messy operational environment and solve it analytically.

 A track record you can point at: specific operational outcomes your work caused, with the numbers, the program, and the skeptics named.

 Experience shipping analytics as supported products with real users, and retiring what they replace.

 Able to influence business unit and functional leadership peer-to-peer without authority, and to work credibly with a program team that starts out unconvinced.

 Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. U.S. person status required per ITAR/EAR.

 
 Preferred qualifications

 
 Operational depth in manufacturing, supply chain, or planning, including fluency with routings, work orders, MRP exceptions, and cycle counts.

 Analytical ownership of a production ramp from low rate to high rate.

 Experience building an analytics function from a scattered starting point, consolidating people, standards, and tooling that previously sat under separate owners.

protected_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Global Material Movement team is responsible for every movement of material from a supplier's dock to the point of use on Anduril's production lines. We receive, inspect, store, count, kit and deliver the parts that build Anduril's products, and we hold custody of government property along the way. The team exists so that production never stops for material. As Anduril adds production lines and new buildings, warehouse capacity limits how fast each new product can ramp. Site Execution and Production Supply is the operating core of that team: the people, the floor and the daily results at Anduril's headquarters and Orange County facilities.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for a Director, Warehouse Operations and Production Supply to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA. In this role, you will be responsible for warehouse and production supply operations across our headquarters and Orange County facilities: receiving, put away, picking, kitting, line side delivery and outbound shipping. You will lead a team of managers and supervisors and several hundred hourly associates, and you will open a new campus in Long Beach. Government property and export controlled material stay in custody the whole way. This will require experience running high volume, multi site warehouse operations by the numbers: labor planned against demand, productivity measured by process, and every miss traced to a root cause. If you are someone who walks the floor before you read the dashboard, can launch a building and get it to rate quickly, and builds supervisors who run their shifts through standard work and continuous improvement, then this role is for you.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 
 Run daily operations across our headquarters and Orange County sites: receiving, put away, storage, picking, kitting, line side delivery, and outbound shipping to other Anduril sites and to deployment.

 Own the result production cares about most: zero line stoppages caused by material, with dock to stock, kit on time and line side fill rate held to the service levels agreed with each production team. Every miss gets an A3 with a root cause, a countermeasure, an owner and a date.

 Run the operation from data. Build the daily view of labor, productivity by process, backlog and service level by site, pulled from the system rather than from spreadsheets, and use it to staff every shift.

 Lead from the floor through daily Gemba walks, tier meetings at every site, and a steady pace of kaizen events that each target a measured problem.

 Own safety and cost at every site you run: zero recordables as the standard, the operating budget for labor, overtime, supplies and equipment, and cost per unit handled reported monthly to Finance.

 Hold transaction discipline and location control in every flow you run, so the counts run by our Inventory Control and Quality Assurance team find nothing to fix. Execute quality at the point of handling: receiving checks, damage prevention and segregation of nonconforming material.

 Keep government furnished property and export controlled material segregated, serialized and traceable in every flow you run.

 Hire, train and develop hourly associates and the supervisors who lead them. Manage labor to the productivity standards and staffing guidelines set for each process, and manage overtime and attrition against plan.

 Launch the Long Beach campus: hire its leaders, write its standard work, and run it to the same measures as headquarters from the first shift.

 Act as the first user of every new system and layout. Test warehouse system changes on the floor before they go live, and accept or reject layout and automation handovers from Material Flow Engineering.

 Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, industrial engineering, business or a related field, OR 15+ years of equivalent operations experience

 12+ years of experience in fulfillment, distribution, 3PL or warehouse operations, including leadership of a high volume site

 6+ years leading managers or supervisors across multiple shifts or sites, with 200+ hourly associates and full ownership of safety, labor and productivity results

 Experience managing labor to engineered or measured productivity standards by process

 Experience running warehouse operations on a warehouse management system

 Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet production milestones

 Ability to travel up to 25% of the time

 This position is based in Costa Mesa, CA and requires being onsite. Remote work not considered. Candidates outside the area must be willing to relocate to Costa Mesa, CA

 U.S. Person status is required, as this position needs access to export controlled material and data

 Launched a new fulfillment, distribution or production supply site from pre opening through steady rate

 Builds own analysis in SQL, Python or a BI tool

 Experience supplying a manufacturing production line through kitting, kanban and line side replenishment

 Aerospace, defense or regulated manufacturing experience, including custody of government furnished property

 Led the operations side of a warehouse management system implementation or migration

 Lean or Six Sigma certification, or a documented record of kaizen results

 Supervisors you hired and developed were later promoted

 Master's degree in supply chain, engineering or business

 Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

Your strategic leadership will ensure the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers worldwide, while meeting ambitious manufacturing throughput requirements. This position demands an exceptional blend of strategic foresight, executive presence, and deep technical acumen to resolve complex testing challenges, drive global scalability, and enhance our automation, uniformity, and data-driven decision-making processes.

 Lead the strategic design, procurement, and implementation of test infrastructure and equipment, ensuring robust capabilities for diverse hardware complexities while optimizing cost-benefit and ROI.

 Champion initiatives that drive operational excellence, including enhancing safety, reducing costs, improving quality, and increasing productivity across all manufacturing test operations.

 Establish robust data analytics frameworks and reporting structures to provide actionable insights for strategic decision-making, continuous product/process enhancement, and performance optimization across the enterprise.

 Implement comprehensive training, documentation, and proactive maintenance strategies to elevate team expertise, facilitate knowledge transfer, and ensure equipment uptime across the global footprint.

 Act as the ultimate technical authority and strategic advisor for all manufacturing test matters, guiding complex problem-solving and long-range planning.

 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field.

 Profound expertise in the testing of complex electro-mechanical assemblies, advanced electrical systems, and propulsion technologies.

 Proven ability to lead, mentor, and inspire large, diverse engineering teams, fostering professional growth and high performance.

 Exceptional executive presence, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical strategies to non-technical audiences.

 Strong financial acumen, including experience managing large departmental budgets and strategic capital expenditures.

 Deep understanding of manufacturing processes, quality systems, and reliability engineering principles in high-volume, fast-paced environments.

 Strong analytical skills for root cause analysis of non-conforming hardware and process deviations.

 Familiarity with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Test Execution Systems (TES).

 Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Advanced degree (Master's or Ph.D.) in a relevant engineering discipline or MBA.

 Proven experience in establishing and expanding global manufacturing test capabilities, including greenfield site development.

 Familiarity with test automation software platforms and programming languages (e.g., Python, C#, LabVIEW, MATLAB) for high-level system integration and data analysis.

 Expertise in designing and specifying test fixtures and equipment for challenging mechanical, electrical, and propulsion components.

 Strong knowledge of reliability and environmental testing (HASS, ESS, thermal cycling, vibration, shock) specifically for advanced physical systems.

 Experience with various hardware communication protocols relevant to complex system integration.

 Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

 The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril's fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are scaling production of autonomous aircraft across our manufacturing facilities. Manufacturing Engineering drives process development, production readiness, and the transition from prototype to rate — ensuring that what Design engineers create can be built reliably, repeatedly, and at scale. 

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 Anduril is seeking a Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering to lead ME strategy and execution across the Autonomous Airpower portfolio. This is not a single-program role — you will be the manufacturing engineering voice across every aircraft program in the portfolio, from early concept through full-rate production. You will work directly with chief engineers, program managers, and the growth team to shape what gets built, how it gets built, and whether it can be built on cost and on schedule. 

 You are the first person from the ME organization that program managers and growth leads turn to when evaluating emerging capabilities. You provide the manufacturing perspective on what is realistic and achievable — grounding engineering ambitions in production reality. You understand every phase of the aircraft lifecycle: DFM input during design, participation in design reviews, prototype and first-article builds, LRIP standup, and the transition to full-rate production. You know what it takes to go from a clean-sheet aircraft concept to hardware rolling off a production line. 

 You will build and lead a team of manufacturing engineers, set the technical direction for the ME organization, and represent manufacturing engineering to directors and executives. This role requires someone who has lived aircraft manufacturing — not managed it from a distance — and who can move fluidly between a factory floor conversation and an executive review. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 
 Lead manufacturing engineering strategy and execution across the full Autonomous Airpower portfolio, spanning multiple aircraft programs in various stages of maturity 

 Serve as the primary ME point of contact for program managers and the growth team on emerging capabilities — providing early-stage assessments of manufacturability, cost, schedule, and production feasibility

 Build, develop, and lead a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers across disciplines — structures, mechanical systems, fluid systems, propulsion, avionics, and harnessing 

 Drive cross-functional alignment between engineering, supply chain, manufacturing operations, program management, quality, and leadership to ensure production readiness across programs

 Represent manufacturing engineering in executive reviews, program gate reviews, and customer-facing discussions, translating production realities into clear, actionable information for senior leadership 

 Establish manufacturing engineering standards, processes, and best practices that scale across programs and production sites 

 Evaluate and advise on make-vs-buy decisions, capital investments, and production strategies based on deep knowledge of aircraft manufacturing capabilities and constraints 

 Drive production readiness across the portfolio — MBOMs, process maturity, tooling readiness, rate-readiness assessments — ensuring programs are set up to succeed at each production milestone

 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering 

 12+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace or defense, with significant time spent on aircraft programs

 Experience across the full aircraft production lifecycle: DFM, design reviews, prototype/first-article builds, LRIP, and full-rate production 

 5+ years of experience leading and developing manufacturing engineering teams 

 Demonstrated ability to assess emerging programs and provide credible manufacturing cost, schedule, and feasibility inputs 

 Experience presenting manufacturing status, risks, and recommendations to director-level and executive audiences 

 Strong cross-functional leadership — proven ability to drive alignment across engineering, operations, supply chain, program management, and business leadership 

 Experience managing manufacturing engineering budgets and cost positions across multiple programs 

 Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance 

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Experience standing up new aircraft production lines from scratch — from facility planning through rate production 

 Experience working directly with growth or business development teams to shape proposals and production strategies for new aircraft programs 

 Experience with autonomous aircraft, UAV, or advanced air vehicle programs 

 Knowledge of EVMS, earned value reporting, and program control fundamentals 

 Experience with Manufacturing Readiness Levels (MRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Assessments (MRA) 

 Experience working with Teamcenter, SAP, Oracle, or similar PLM/ERP platforms 

 Master's degree in Engineering, Business, or related field 

 Active U.S. Secret security clearance

 Experience in unit-level/space vehicle/system integration, assembly, and environmental testing (eg., vibration, thermal vacuum, acoustic, shock, and EMI/EMC)

 Background in integration and testing of avionics/optical payloads, solar, propulsion, ADCS, or other space hardware.

 Proven team leadership skills, with examples of successfully managing and developing a diverse team.

 Familiarity with CAD software, Manufacturing Execution systems, and ERP/MRP systems.

 A genuine interest in manufacturing and a thirst for learning, particularly in the space domain.

 Demonstrated success in scaling product testing and production from one to tens/hundreds.

 Active security clearance or ability to obtain a security clearance.

 Experience in test hardware and software development

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 
Anduril’s Manufacturing Safety Engineering team partners across Anduril’s manufacturing, engineering, and operations organizations to ensure our production systems are safe to build, test, and sustain at scale. As an engineering discipline, we design safety into the way products are made, covering the equipment, fixtures, test stations, and work instructions on the factory floor, rather than inspecting for it after the fact. Our mandate spans the production lifecycle, from new equipment and line design through ramp and sustained operations. We apply formal risk assessment and the hierarchy of controls to identify hazards early and engineer them out, partnering closely with our Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) experts, controls and manufacturing engineers, and production leadership to keep our people safe while moving at the speed Anduril demands.

 ABOUT THE JOB 
We are seeking an experienced Manufacturing Safety Engineering leader to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA to stand up and scale manufacturing safety as an engineering discipline across Anduril. This is a build role: you will create the manufacturing-safety-engineering team, define the risk-assessment framework and processes that keep our production equipment, fixtures, test stations, and work instructions safe, and drive adoption of those practices across Anduril’s manufacturing sites. As a Manufacturing Safety leader, you will apply deep expertise in machine safety, formal risk assessment, and the hierarchy of controls to engineer hazards out of how our products are built, partnering closely with EHS, manufacturing and controls engineering, and production leadership. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical leader who can set strategy and standards while remaining the senior authority on the hardest hazard problems on the floor.
This role is based in Costa Mesa, CA, and supports Anduril’s manufacturing operations, including sites at Quonset Point, RI and Atlanta, GA; travel to production sites is expected.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 
 Build, lead, and develop the Manufacturing Safety Engineering team, including hiring, leveling, mentoring, and performance management, as the discipline scales across Anduril.

 Establish and standardize the manufacturing-safety framework: risk-assessment methodology, templates, risk-acceptance criteria, safety sign-off gates, and the management-of-change process, aligned to the business.

 Grow the manufacturing-safety discipline across Anduril, driving adoption across production lines and sites and defining the standards of record, in partnership with Manufacturing, EHS, and product engineering.

 Define and communicate the discipline’s vision, goals, roadmap, and operating model, and integrate manufacturing-safety practices across all stages of production development.

 Own manufacturing-safety metrics, KPIs, and executive-level reporting; represent the discipline to leadership and to customer and defense-program stakeholders.

 Manage resource allocation and capacity planning across concurrent programs and sites, and manage budget, tooling, and external partnerships (EHS, controls integrators, certification bodies).

 Serve as the senior technical authority and final risk-acceptance escalation point for the highest-consequence manufacturing hazards.

 Lead formal machine and task-based risk assessments on production equipment, fixtures, tooling, and processes, documenting hazards, risk ratings, required controls, and residual risk.

 Review manufacturing work instructions and supporting training material for safety adequacy; author Job Hazard Analyses (JHA) and embed the required controls, PPE, and safe-work steps.

 Engineer and review production equipment such as lift fixtures and material-handling aids in partnership with EHS, and support proof-load testing.

 Assess and design safety into production test equipment.

 Apply the hierarchy of controls and prevention-through-design principles to eliminate or reduce hazards at the equipment and line-design stage.

 Define functional-safety requirements for safety-related control systems and verify their implementation.

 Partner with EHS to ensure engineering controls satisfy applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, electrical, PPE, materials handling).

 Support incident and near-miss investigations and root-cause analysis; drive corrective engineering actions and management of change.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 B.S. Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or Safety Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline

 10+ years of experience in manufacturing/machine safety, equipment/controls engineering, or a related discipline, with at least 3 years in a leadership role

 Proven track record building, scaling, and managing technical teams and establishing engineering processes or disciplines

 Deep expertise in formal machine and task-based risk assessment and machine safeguarding, applied across equipment, fixtures, and processes

 Strong working knowledge of applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, electrical, PPE, materials handling) as engineering controls

 Experience partnering with EHS, manufacturing, and design organizations to embed safety into equipment and production processes

 Strategic thinking with the ability to balance hands-on technical authority with organizational leadership responsibilities

 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence cross-functionally at all levels

 Eligibility to pursue and maintain a U.S. security clearance, as required

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Familiarity with machine safety standards such as ISO 12100 (risk assessment and risk reduction), ISO 13849 (safety-related parts of control systems), and ANSI B11 (machine safety and safeguarding)

 M.S. Degree in an engineering discipline

 Professional safety or machinery-safety certification (CSP, CMSE)

 12+ years of experience with at least 5 years in a leadership role, including standing up a safety-engineering function or discipline from an early stage

 Experience managing teams and programs across multiple manufacturing sites, and through periods of rapid growth (2x+ expansion)

 Track record of developing talent and promoting team members into senior and leadership roles

 Experience in high-rate or rapidly scaling aerospace, defense, or automotive manufacturing

 Executive-level communications, reporting, and roadmap presentation experience

 Active U.S. security clearance

 US Salary Range
 $166,000 — $220,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

 ABOUT THE TEAM  

We are seeking a highly experienced and dynamic Senior Manager, Test Operations   to lead our Development and Production Testing efforts across multiple critical space programs. 

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 Anduril's Space business is standing up manufacturing and test for multiple space vehicle lines at once — moving from development builds today into full rate production within four years. The Senior Manager, Test Operations will build and lead the test organization that makes that ramp possible: vehicle and subassembly acceptance and qualification test, environmental test operations, test station and ground support equipment engineering, and the procedures and data systems behind them.

 This is a build role, not a sustaining one. The production test organization does not exist yet — you will define it, hire it, and stand up its capability inside a new production facility whose environmental test infrastructure is still being defined. Test throughput and cost-effectiveness are the binding constraint on our production rate; architecture decisions defined today will have lasting impacts to production rate success.

 Test Organization and Leadership 

 
 Recruit, mentor and lead a multi-domain test organization spanning functional and electrical test, environmental test, test station and GSE engineering, and test operations — growing from initial hires toward a projected 40+ positions through the production ramp.

 Own the transfer of test knowledge, procedures and tooling from development-site test engineers into the production test team, including training, certification and proficiency standards for test engineers and technicians.

 Coordinate closely with Launch Operations stakeholders to ensure all System Test procedures, resources, and approval criteria are followed during launch campaigns. As needed, deployed Test personnel to support, train, and oversee launch operations to ensure compliance.

 
 Test Campaign Definition and Execution 

 
 Define and own vehicle-level and subassembly acceptance test procedures and qualification campaigns, including test flow, entrance and exit criteria, and data review gates.

 Lead Test Readiness Reviews and test campaign readiness assessments; serve as approval authority for test procedures run on flight hardware.

 Own environmental test execution — thermal vacuum, sine and random vibration, acoustic, shock, thermal cycling, and EMI/EMC — including chamber and table scheduling, fixture and instrumentation readiness, and anomaly disposition.

 
 Design for Test 

 
 Drive design-for-test requirements into vehicle, payload and subassembly designs before CDR, with the explicit objective of reducing test duration and test station count at rate.

 Challenge inherited test requirements: identify tests that can be combined, moved to a lower assembly level, automated, or eliminated at acceptable risk, and carry those cases through the requirement owners with data.

 
 Capability, Facility and Rate 

 
 Specify production environmental test capability — chamber count and size, vibration table capacity, EMI/EMC screen rooms — and own the test capacity model behind it.

 Represent test operations up and out: support proposal development and Basis of Estimate content for test scope, present at technical and milestone reviews, and brief customers and business line leadership on test readiness, capability and risk.

 
 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics or a related technical field.

 10+ years in spacecraft or space vehicle integration and test, including 5+ years leading test engineers or technicians, and technical lead or manager on at least two complete environmental qualification or acceptance campaigns from procedure definition through data review and disposition.

 Hands-on ownership of at least three of: thermal vacuum, sine or random vibration, acoustic, shock, thermal cycling, EMI/EMC to MIL-STD-461 or equivalent.

 Managed a team of 10 or more engineers and/or technicians spanning at least two test domains — for example functional and electrical test plus environmental test, or test operations plus test station engineering.

 Working knowledge of a recognized space test standard such as SMC-S-016, GSFC-STD-7000 (GEVS) or MIL-STD-1540, including where you tailored it and why.

 Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

 
 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 A quantified improvement in test throughput or cycle time that you can explain mechanically — for example scaling test capacity by 3x or more, or reducing test flow duration by 20% or more.

 Authored or approved 10 or more test procedures executed on flight hardware.

 Has represented a test or manufacturing organization up and out: contributed to proposal and Basis of Estimate content, and briefed customers or executive leadership on readiness and risk. Both the written and the in-person sides matter here.

 Stood up an environmental test capability or a test organization from zero — chamber and table procurement, commissioning, facility interface, first-article campaigns.

 Took a spacecraft or complex electromechanical product from single-digit annual builds into rate production of 100+ units per year.

 Supported space vehicle test through to Launch and Operations

 Python scripting and test automation; experience with automated test execution and test data pipelines.

 Operated in both classified and unclassified cleanroom environments.

 Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret or U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

 Intelligence Systems is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements. As the Sr. Manager of Manufacturing Test Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of production systems to support high-volume products across the portfolio. You are charged with ensuring rigorous testing protocols are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Furthermore, your leadership guarantees the fulfillment of manufacturing's test throughput requirements. This position demands an innovative approach to resolving complex testing challenges, advancing scalability, and enhancing our automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics methodologies.

 This role will be based temporarily at Santa Ana, CA for a 3 month training period before transitioning to Asheville, OH. 

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 
 Direct the manufacturing test engineering team, set objectives, guide initiatives, and assess team outcomes.

 Architect and oversee the manufacturing test strategy for each product to ensure scalable operations across Anduril, transitioning from pre-production to full-scale output.

 Strategize and implement advancements in manufacturing testing, focusing on automation, uniformity, and operational streamlining.

 Evaluate test data, compile findings, and identify opportunities for product and process enhancements.

 Communicate strategic visions to key stakeholders, guiding the scaling of platforms from pre-production (LRIP) through to mass production (FRP).

 Collaborate with product development for design testability, ensuring seamless production integration.

 Lead the procurement and implementation of new test equipment, performing cost-benefit and ROI analyses as needed.

 Champion initiatives that enhance safety, reduce costs, improve quality, and increase productivity through testing.

 Cultivate a culture focused on innovation, collaboration, and accountability in the engineering department.

 Act as the go-to technical authority for manufacturing test matters, advising on and troubleshooting complex issues.

 Design proactive maintenance and calibration protocols for manufacturing test equipment.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

 Minimum of 8 years of relevant industry experience leading manufacturing test engineering.

 Expertise in Linux, C#, Python, and NixOS.

 Solid experience with PCBA/electronic assembly testing and knowledge of testing standards.

 Proficiency in using electronic test equipment.

 Strong analytical skills for root cause analysis of non-conforming hardware.

 Familiar with Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Test Execution Systems (TES)

 Experience in managing projects that integrate electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems.

 Active U.S. Secret security clearance

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Advanced degree in a relevant engineering discipline.

 Demonstrated ability to lead the development of manufacturing test systems and teams.

 Proficiency in LabVIEW, MATLAB, and test automation.

 Knowledge of PCBA design, mechanical design, and ESS testing.

 Familiarity with various hardware communication protocols.

 Experience with HASS & ESS-related testing (Thermal, Vibration, etc.)

protected_roles.title: VP Production, Connected Warfare
protected_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE ROLE 
The Vice President, Production, Connected Warfare provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for all production activities within Anduril's Connected Warfare organization. Connected Warfare builds the compute, comms, and infrastructure products that modern defense programs rely on a business growing toward multi-billion-dollar scale, producing integrated hardware and software products at real volume. Encompassing production planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, and manufacturing operations, this role will be responsible for production across multiple business lines and multiple facilities. The VP orchestrates a portfolio of production programs, making resource allocation tradeoffs, and setting the Connected Warfare production strategy. This executive is responsible for driving operational excellence and production efficiency in the near term and building the production capabilities necessary to support Connected Warfare's and the company's long-term business objectives . 


 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 
 Establish and provide strategic and operational leadership across multiple production facilities - ensuring consistency in quality, cost, and delivery performance across geographies

 Lead and build the production capabilities of a portfolio of products, balancing investment, capacity, and talent allocation across product lines and production programs

 Partner with R&D, sales, and engineering teams to lead new product introduction efforts across multiple emerging product lines, developing from scratch the production lines and processes necessary to meet our customers’ requirements

 Drive division-level production strategy including facility footprint decisions, make-vs-buy analyses, capital deployment planning, and workforce sizing aligned to multi-year business forecasts. 

 Establish the operational excellence framework and continuous improvement culture across the division, leveraging lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies to reduce costs, improve yields, and increase throughput

 Establish and monitor KPIs across safety, quality, delivery, schedule, and cost to ensure performance targets are met across multiple production sites, including international expansions

 Build and develop a high-performing production organization through talent development and a strong culture of accountability

 Support capital planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for production functions across the division

 Ensure compliance with all regulatory, environmental, health, and safety requirements

 Lead capacity planning and footprint strategy, including evaluation of new facilities and/or manufacturing technologies

 Serve as a member of the division's senior leadership team, contributing to division and corporate strategic planning; represent the production organization in executive, customer, and investor contexts as appropriate

 Collaborate in a matrix environment with strong relationships and influence ability across multiple stakeholders across the business

 Lead workforce and location strategy, including labor market analysis, site selection criteria, and workforce sizing, to support new line stand-ups and geographic expansion

 
 QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred

 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, with at least 7-10 years in a senior or executive role overseeing organizations of 500+ employees; experience in a high- or hyper-growth environment

 Proven track record of leading large, complex manufacturing operations across multiple sites or locations

 Experience managing simultaneous product ramps across multiple facilities and scaling international manufacturing operations required

 Experience across all 5 pillars of production: production planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, operations, and quality

 Demonstrated ability to set and scale an operational excellence framework across a division, with deep expertise in lean manufacturing and continuous improvement

 Prior experience managing large budgets in the hundreds of millions of dollars and capital programs

 Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills

 Experience in regulated industries (e.g., defense, automotive, aerospace, medical devices) a plus

 Direct P&L ownership in a production environment with demonstrated ability to manage financial performance at division scale

 Executive presence and sophisticated communication skills; proven ability to influence C-suite stakeholders, represent the production function externally, and shape corporate-level strategy

 
  
 US Salary Range
 $252,000 — $382,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.
